Among the fragrances of virtues and the sweet scent of holy pursuits, the balm of your reputation is distinguished to us by its own fragrance; since it separates itself from worldly vanity by more austere observances and shines with the splendid glory of merits, it deserves greater honour from us. Accordingly, care must be taken more diligently and precautions made lest anyone’s wickedness should be able to disturb that holy tranquillity. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, [Col. 1339B] moved by your humble petition, by these present letters we grant that, whenever clerics or laymen of a lower religious order decide to enter the profession of your order, you may freely receive them by our permission and retain them once they have made profession with you, saving, nevertheless, privileges obtained from the Apostolic See on this matter. But if one of those possessing such a privilege remains with you for a year after the brethren of the house have learned from which order he departed, without being reclaimed there, he may thereafter neither abandon your order nor be forcibly recalled from it. You may also seek consecration of churches and ordination of clerics from any bishop, if you cannot obtain your own bishop or if, when asked, he refuses to provide it as he ought; and the bishop so asked, coming to your churches, may, relying on our authority, provide you with the sacred things required. [Col. 1339C] You too, beloved son Prior, may restrain by sentence of excommunication those who, from your order, take occasions for wandering—whether under pretext of assisting the Holy Land or for any other cause—if, having been admonished, they do not decide to abandon that purpose.

Let no person whatsoever therefore be permitted to infringe this charter of our grant and constitution or rashly oppose it. But whoever presumes to attempt this shall know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

[Col. 1339D] Given at the Lateran, on the second day before the Ides of April, in the first year of our pontificate.

LI. He takes the monastery of Saint Benedict of Gualdo under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. (Lateran, 6 May.)

[MITTARELLI, *Annal. Camaldul.*, IV, Appendix, p. 168.]

Clement, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Senebald, abbot of the monastery of Saint Benedict of Waldo, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

Those who choose the religious life ought to have apostolic protection at hand, lest perhaps the assault of any rashness either recall them from their purpose or [Col. 1340A]—God forbid!—weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and we receive under the protection of Saint Peter and of ourselves, after the example of Nicholas, Celestine, Eugenius, Adrian, and Alexander, Roman pontiffs of blessed memory, our predecessors, and strengthen by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid monastery of Saint Benedict of Waldo, which is specially of the right of the Roman Church and in which you are devoted to divine service. First, indeed, we establish that the monastic order known to have been instituted in your monastery according to God, the Rule of Saint Benedict, and the institution of the Camaldolese brethren, shall there be observed inviolate for all time.

[Col. 1340B] Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the Lord’s favor, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The place itself in which the aforesaid monastery is situated, with its parish church and all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Martin of Collis; the church of Saint Nicholas of Capriano; the church of Saint Christopher of Bantiara; the right which you possess in the church of the castle of Valle; the church of Saint Lawrence of Saxo [Col. 1340C] sp[lacuna]; the church of Saint Mary of Fricco; the church of Saint John of Castellano; the church of Saint Mary of Umbracia, with half the estate; the church of Saint Nicholas of Vultule; the church of Saint Sabinus of Serra; the church of Saint Angel of Fabrica; the church of Saint Angel of Flea; whatever you possess in the church of Saint Mary of Noscano; the church of Saint Angel of Terrasicca; the right which you possess in the church of Saint Cassian of Palatiolo; the church of Saint Martin of Valle Vajeria; the right which you possess in the church of Saint George of Corneto; the church of Saint Lawrence of Collebassani; the church of Saint Peter of Collebassani; the church of Saint Peter of Crucicle; the church of Saint Paternian of Corrutone; the church of Saints Gregory and John of Serraradica; [Col. 1340D] the church of Saint John of Serrapila; the church of Saint Victorinus near Nebula; the church of Saint Paul of Cavalalx; the church of Saint Peter of Roccacontrada; the church of Saint Peter of Monte Boddo; the church of Saint Stephen of la Calcinaria, with all the appurtenances of the aforesaid churches.

Furthermore, no one shall presume to extort tithes from you on your newly cleared lands, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or from [lacuna] of your animals. You may also receive into conversion clerics or laymen, free and unencumbered, fleeing from the world, and retain them without any opposition. Moreover, we forbid any of your brethren, after making profession in that place, [Col. 1341A] to leave it without his abbot’s permission, unless for the sake of a stricter religious life; and no one shall dare retain those who depart without letters of the community attesting this. When a general interdict has been imposed upon the land, you may celebrate the divine offices with closed doors, excluding excommunicated and interdicted persons, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordination of your clerics who are to be promoted to holy orders from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is catholic, enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to provide these things freely and without any improper demand. Otherwise, you may approach whichever catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested. Furthermore, we decree that the burial-place of that house shall be free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion and last will of those who choose to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or interdicted; without prejudice, nevertheless, to the right of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken.

Upon the death of yourself, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it through any craft of usurpation or by force, except the person whom the brethren, by common consent, or the sounder counsel of the brethren, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Benedict. Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever, etc.

I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1341C] I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Melior, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement. I, Bobo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Alexander, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Peter in Chains. I, Radulf, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Hyacinth, cardinal priest of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. [Col. 1341D] I, G. G., cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Soffredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, John Felix, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace beside the Temple of Agrippa. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Bernard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary Nova. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Brother Moses, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church, acting in place of the chancellor, on the second day before the Nones of May, in the sixth indiction, in the year 1188 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

## LII. He confirms a judgment rendered in the presence of Urban III between the sisters of Saint Hilary and the provost of Florence. (Lateran, 6 May.)

[Ibid., p. 171.]

[Col. 1342A]

Clement, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, the abbess and sisters of Saint Hilary: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have learned from a certain authentic instrument presented to us that, whereas a dispute concerning certain tithes was being litigated between you and our beloved son the provost of Florence, and the case had been entrusted by Urban, our predecessor of happy memory, to our beloved sons the priors of Camaldoli and of the Holy Apostles, they, after the parties had appeared before them and the arguments on either side had been heard and examined, pronounced judgment in favor of you and your church concerning those tithes. Since controversies which receive a definitive decision by apostolic mandate ought fittingly to obtain perpetual force, we confirm by apostolic authority the judgment itself, as reasonably rendered, not suspended by a lawful appeal, and contained in an authentic written instrument, and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. Therefore let no person whatsoever, etc. If anyone, etc.

Given at the Lateran, on the second day before the Nones of May, in the first year of our pontificate.

## LIII. Privilege for the church of Saint John of Monza. (Lateran, 15 May.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, IV, 62.]

[Col. 1342C]

Clement, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Oberto, archpriest of Monza, and his brethren, present and future, canonically appointed, for ever.

A pious request ought to be brought to completion by the fulfillment of the will, so that both the sincerity of devotion may shine forth laudably and the requested benefit may assuredly gain force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your requests; and, after the example of our predecessors of blessed memory, Callixtus, Innocent, [Col. 1342D] Celestine, Anastasius, and Alexander, Roman pontiffs, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present writing, the church of Blessed John the Baptist of Monza, in which you are devoted to divine service. We establish that whatever possessions and goods that same church justly and peaceably possessed up to the time when our predecessor Lord Urban was elevated, or may hereafter, by the Lord’s favor, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the church of Saint John the Baptist itself, with all its chapels and appurtenances; namely, the churches [Col. 1343A] of Saint Michael, Saint Savior, Saint Peter, Saint Victor, Saint Lawrence with its hospital, Saint Alexander of Blandino, Saint Martin, Saint Blaise, Saint Agatha, Saint Maurice with its hospital, Saint Ambrose, Saint Donatus with its hospital, Saint Fidelis, and Saint Anastasia in Dotano; the churches of Saint Carpophorus and Saint Mary of Surturi in Sesto; the churches of Saint Alexander, Saint Savior, Saint Michael, Saint Eusebius, Saint Mary of Teneblavo, and Saint Mary of Sundri; the parish church of Saint Julian of Colonia with all its chapels, namely that at Albariat; the churches of Saint Martin and Saint Maurice in the village of Modroni; the church of Saint Remigius in Colonia; the churches of Saint Gregory and Saint Nazarius in Caliate; the churches of Saint Carpophorus and Saint Alexandrinus, with a hospital, in Concoretio; the church of Saint Eugenius in Valate; the churches of Saint Mary and Saint Fidelis [Col. 1343B] in Clamella; the church of Saint Sisinnius; and the monastery of Saint Peter.

We likewise confirm for you the confirmation of the election of the abbess of Cremella, as it was reasonably granted to you and confirmed by his writing by Robald, late archbishop of Milan, of good memory; and also the right and reasonable customs which you possess in that church of Blessed Peter at Cremella. We likewise confirm for you the church of Saint Gregory in Ormano; at Blociano, the church of Saint John; Saint Gregory of Calciago; Saint John of Varena; Saint Mary of Sara; Saint Peter of Sirone; Saint John of Castro Marcio; the tithe of the whole territory of Monza; the tithe of the whole territory of Sesto, except the tithe of Tenebioco; [Col. 1343C] the entire tithe from the territory of Coliate; the tithe of Concoretio; the tithe accruing from places of the parish of Colonia, namely from the locality of Colonia, from the locality of the village of Modroni, and from the locality of Albatiate; and the principal estates, namely the court or manor of Cremella, the court of Bruciati, the court of Varena, the court of Castro Martis, the court of Lauredi, the court of Calphurii, and the court of Leucate, to you and, through you, to your church.

Furthermore, we strengthen by apostolic authority for you and your successors those feudal benefices which Jordan, formerly archbishop of Milan, of reverend memory, discreetly granted to your church in the above-named churches for the common support of the brethren; and we forbid any person whatsoever henceforth to remove, withdraw, or alter them in any way from their usefulness for the brethren in common. Moreover, we declare ratified the ancient liberties and immunities and the reasonable customs granted to your church, as well as those confirmed by our aforesaid predecessors and observed until the time of the elevation of the aforementioned Urban, our predecessor; and we decree that they shall remain unimpaired in future times, notwithstanding anything that may reasonably have been altered contrary to the grant and confirmation of the aforesaid Roman pontiffs. Furthermore, we forbid anyone within your parish to presume to build a new church or chapel without your consent, saving the privileges of the Roman pontiffs. Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever [Col. 1344A] may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, etc., saving in all things the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical enactments of the archbishop of Milan. If therefore anyone, etc. Amen.

I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Melior, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, Radulf, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. [Col. 1344B] I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement. I, Bobo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Alexius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Soffredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, John Felix, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace beside the Temple of Agrippa.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Brother Moses, subdeacon of the Roman [Col. 1344C] Church, acting in place of the chancellor, on the Ides of May, in the sixth indiction, in the year 1188 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

## LIV. Privilege for the church of Saint Germanus. (Lateran, 17 May.)

[TOSTI, *History of Monte Cassino*, II, 211, from the original.]

Clement, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons John, archpriest of the church of Saint Germanus, and the clerics, present and future, canonically appointed, for ever.

The force of equity and the order of reason require that effect be granted to just petitioners, especially when piety assists the petitioners’ wish and truth does not abandon it. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and, following in the footsteps of Alexander, pope of happy memory, our predecessor, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid church of Saint Germanus, in which you are devoted to divine service. We establish that whatever possessions and goods that same church presently justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the Lord’s favor, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Furthermore, because the sacred canons [Col. 1345A] provide that no priest, deacon, subdeacon, or cleric of whatever rank shall be dragged before the tribunal of a secular judge, we enact and establish by apostolic authority, as Gerard, formerly abbot of Monte Cassino, of good memory, decreed with the consent of his brethren, that no cleric dwelling in the whole territory of Saint Benedict shall be bound by secular judgment, be judged by any lay person, or be compelled to make purgation, undergo an ordeal, give a pledge, or furnish a surety. But if any of the aforesaid clerics falls into any crime or fault, or if any crime is alleged against him, he shall be judged by you, son archpriest, or by your successors appointed by the abbot of Saint Benedict, [Col. 1345B] and not by public judges. Yet, when circumstances require and it is necessary, the advice and permission of that same abbot shall be sought in this matter, as is known to have been granted to you in his authentic written instrument.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, remove its possessions, retain those removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See, the canonical right of the abbot of Monte Cassino, and due reverence. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person shall henceforth knowingly attempt to act against this page of our constitution, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offense by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ; and, at the last judgment, let him be subject to strict punishment. But upon all who preserve their rights to that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint [Col. 1345D] Mark. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Bobo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, James, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Soffredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Bobo, cardinal deacon of Saint Gregory at the Golden Veil. [Col. 1346A] I, G. G., cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church, acting in place of the chancellor, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of June, in the sixth indiction, in the year 1188 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

## LV. He informs the consuls and people of Pisa that Peter, cardinal priest of Saint Cecilia, and Soffredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have been sent to settle their dispute with the Genoese over Sardinia. (Lateran, 19 May.)

[TRONCI, *Memories of Pisa*, 151.]

[Col. 1346B]

Clement, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the consuls and people of Pisa: greeting and apostolic blessing.

For the calming of injuries and the settling of disputes which, at the instigation of the enemy of humankind, have sprung up between you and the Genoese from times long past on account of Sardinia, we have decided, with the counsel and consent of our brethren, to send to those regions our beloved sons P., cardinal priest of the church of Saint Cecilia, and S., cardinal deacon of Saint Mark [read: Saint Mary] in Via Lata—men indeed prudent and discreet. Therefore, in order that henceforth every obstacle to agreement in this matter may be allayed [Col. 1346C] and that, with the Lord as author, no material for scandal may arise, we command and enjoin your whole community, under the obligation of the oath which you have given us in this matter, to receive as spoken from our own mouth and observe inviolably and without any contradiction the commands which the aforesaid cardinals shall issue to you on our behalf concerning all the articles; knowing that we have given the same command to the Genoese under a like sanction.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of June, in the first year of our pontificate.

## LVI. He commands Tammo, bishop of Verden, the abbot of Lüne, and the master of schools of Verden not to permit a certain estate to be taken from the nuns of Levene by Hartwig, archbishop of Hamburg. (Lateran, 25 May.)

[LAPPENBERG, *Hamburg Charters*, I, 244.]

[Col. 1346D]

Clement, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to …, bishop of Verden, and to his beloved sons, the abbot of Lüne and the master of schools of Verden: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have received the representation of our beloved daughters in Christ, the nuns of the church of Saint Vitus at Quivena, that Sifrid, formerly archbishop of Bremen, granted them in perpetual possession, after the death of a certain widowed woman who holds it, and with her consent, a certain estate with its appurtenances belonging to the church of Bremen; [Col. 1347A] and that he forbade anyone, under threat of anathema, to presume to contravene his act. Yet our venerable brother H., his successor, although he decreed that this should obtain force, is nevertheless acting contrary to his own confirmation and threat of anathema and is endeavoring to invalidate that donation. Since we owe them the firmer support in their right because they render their service to Christ more devotedly, we command you by apostolic letters that, if the matter stands thus, you shall cause that donation, as reasonably made, to be firmly and unimpairedly observed by our authority, restraining by ecclesiastical censure those who presume to act against it. If all of you cannot take part in carrying this out, nevertheless let two of you carry it out.

Given at the Lateran, on the eighth day before the Kalends of June, in the first year of our pontificate.

## LVII. Privilege for the Church of Ravello. (Lateran, 29 May.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, I, 1186.]

Clement, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother John, bishop of Ravello, and his successors canonically appointed, for ever.

Since, by the office of the apostolate entrusted to us by God, through which, by the Lord’s appointment, we stand above all Christ’s faithful, and, as it is contained word for word in the privilege of Lucius III [Col. 1347C] [Note: [Col. 1347] See volume CCI of the *Patrologia*, under Lucius III, no. 68.]. At the end, the subscriptions of the pope and cardinals are found.

I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Melior, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, Ruffinus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Bobo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasius. I, Alexius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Peter in Chains. [Col. 1347D] I, Jordan, cardinal priest of Saint Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor. I, James, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, John, cardinal deacon of the church of Saint Eustace. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Bernard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary Nova. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro.

[Col. 1348A] Given at the Lateran through the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church, acting in place of the chancellor, on the fourth day before the Kalends of June, in the seventh indiction, in the year 1188 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

## LVIII. At Bishop Balderam’s request, he receives the Church of Brandenburg under protection and confirms its goods and rights. (Lateran, 29 May.)

[RIEDEL, *Codex diplomaticus Brandenburgensis*, vol. I, part VIII, p. 119.]

Clement, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Balderam, bishop of Brandenburg, and his successors canonically appointed, for ever.

[Col. 1348B] Placed, by the Lord’s ordering, upon the exalted watchtower of the Apostolic See, we ought to love our brothers and fellow bishops, whether near or far, with fraternal charity, and to provide with paternal solicitude for the churches entrusted to them by God. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, we graciously assent to your just requests; and we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid Church of Brandenburg, over which by God’s authority you are known to preside. We establish that whatever possessions and goods that same Church of Brandenburg now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, [Col. 1348C] offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, acquire by the Lord’s favor, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The northern half of the city of Brandenburg; the northern half of the whole island on which the city itself is built; half of all the villages belonging thereto; likewise, in their entirety, the two towns called Pritzerwe and Elzeri, with all their appurtenances; the provinces of Moraciani, Zierfwifti, Ploni, Zpriavani, Heveldun, Vuueri, Riacani, Zamcici, Dassia, and Lusici, granted to your church by the emperors Otto and Henry of illustrious memory; also the whole tithe of the entire parish of Brandenburg, [Col. 1348D] except the tithes of the possessions of the Church of Magdeburg, which that Church of Magdeburg acquired by exchange through the efforts of Conrad, archbishop of Magdeburg, of good memory, and Wiger, bishop of Brandenburg, in the time of Pope Innocent, our predecessor of happy memory, and King Conrad.

Furthermore, we confirm by apostolic authority the market, mint, toll, jurisdiction, and all other things lawfully and legally belonging thereto, situated at Urslebe, in the district of Northuringa and in the county of Count Liuttere; likewise the established boundaries of the bishopric of Brandenburg: eastward to the River Oder; westward and southward to the River Elbe; and northward [Col. 1349A] to the boundaries of the above-named provinces of Vuueri, Riaciani, and Dacia. Moreover, we strengthen by the protection of this present writing for you and your successors the ancient and reasonable customs hitherto observed, as well as the immunities and liberties granted concerning the election of advocates throughout the bishopric of Brandenburg and concerning other bishops of Brandenburg, which the bishops of Brandenburg have held hitherto.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance [Col. 1349B] and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and due reverence toward the archbishop of Magdeburg. If therefore anyone shall henceforth, etc.

(L. S.)

I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Then follow the subscriptions of thirteen cardinals.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Brother Moses, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church, acting in place of the chancellor, on the fourth day before the Kalends of July, in the sixth indiction, in the year 1188 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

## LIX. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the chapter of Brandenburg. (Lateran, 29 May.)

[Ibid., p. 117.]

[Col. 1349C]

Clement, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Henry, provost of the Church of Brandenburg, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

Beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid Church of Brandenburg, in which you are devoted to divine service. First, indeed, we establish that the canonical order known to have been instituted in that church according to God, the Rule of Blessed Augustine, and the institution of the Premonstratensian Order [Col. 1349D] shall there be observed inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the Lord’s favor, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The place itself in which the aforesaid church is situated, with all its appurtenances; the church of Blessed Godehard at Pardewin and that of Blessed Nicholas at Encherbereh; the church of Saint Mary on Harlungeberg, with a third part of the tithes from the adjoining vineyards; also the villages of Bukowe, Garceliz, Bultiz, Kik, Museltiz, and Gorne, with their tithes and all their appurtenances—cultivated and uncultivated land, woods, marshes, and every useful right—together with the two lakes situated between Gorne and Solve; likewise the villages granted to your church by Margrave Otto and his sons Otto and Henry, namely Muezoe, Tremene, and Thure, with their tithes and all their appurtenances; the church at Thure, with a third part of the tithes of the villages belonging to it, namely Izin, Crelin, Bauwerstorp, and whatever villages may be there; one hundred hides situated at Zucha, which the aforesaid Prince Otto offered, with all their appurtenances, for the soul of his father, mother, and wife Judith the Marchioness, with the consent of their sons; [Col. 1350B] five measures of salt of the larger measure, to be paid annually; moreover the village called Dambe, surrendered by Rudolph of Jericho to Margrave Otto for the use of the church and offered by him and his sons, with all its appurtenances, to our church; the tithes of that village, granted by Bishop Wilmar for your uses; likewise the mill at Clinke; six plots of building land in the city of Pardewin offered by the faithful; the church of Ceclowe with its endowment, namely two hides and all the tithes of that village, and a third part of the tithes of the villages belonging to it; the church at Golitz with its endowment, namely two hides; the church of Verchiecere with its endowment, namely two hides; the church at Nibede with its endowment, namely two hides and a third [Col. 1350C] part of the tithes both of these villages and of the village of Vachowa belonging to Golitz; the whole village of Plussin, situated in Zuche, with all its appurtenances and the entire tithe of that village; the chapel of Marzana, belonging to the church of Verchiecere, with its endowment, namely one hide; the village of Sconelo, in which there are thirty hides, with the entire tithe and all its appurtenances; the care of souls in the city of Brandenburg, which pertains to you by right of the episcopal see, as Bishops Wilmarius, Sifrid, and Balderam granted it to you; and the care of souls in the churches which belong, or shall hereafter belong, to your use.

Furthermore, we confirm by apostolic authority for you and your church all the rights which your church, according to the custom of the other churches [Col. 1350D] of Saxony, justly and peaceably possesses; and especially we have thought fit to confirm by apostolic authority the ancient and reasonable customs of your church hitherto observed. Upon the death of the bishop of that church, we decree that you shall have the first voice in electing his successor; and no one shall be set over you against your will by fraud or force. Rather, the man shall hold the place and office of bishop in your church whom you shall determine to elect from the body of that church, either by unanimous will or on the counsel of the greater and sounder part. But if no suitable person can be found in your church, you shall have permission to elect a suitable person from another church.

Moreover, we establish that you, son provost, and your successors shall hold in perpetuity, undivided and in no way diminished, the archdeaconry of Brandenburg—namely Kytin and Juterbuch and the land of Havela eastward as far as the Oder, and likewise westward as far as the water called Yla—as the provosts of your church have hitherto justly and without dispute held it.

We also forbid anyone within your boundaries, whether in the burial due to your church or in other things which you have hitherto justly and peaceably possessed, to dare rashly to disturb the rights of that church. Finally, by apostolic authority we prohibit parish priests of your diocese from presuming, contrary to the custom of the other cathedral sees [Col. 1351B] of Saxony and to your own, to intrude themselves into elections of bishops.

Furthermore, no one shall presume to demand or extort tithes from you on your lands which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or from the increase of your animals. You may also receive into conversion clerics or laymen fleeing from the world, free and unencumbered, and retain them without any opposition. Moreover, we forbid any of your brethren, after making profession in your house, to leave it without his provost’s permission; and no one shall dare retain one who departs without letters of the community attesting this. In your own causes, whether they involve a civil or criminal question, you may bring forward your brethren who are suitable to testify, and by their testimony, as is right, both repel violence and vindicate justice.

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, remove its possessions, retain those removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person shall henceforth, etc.

[Col. 1351D] I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church.

(The subscriptions of eleven cardinals follow.)

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church, acting in place of the chancellor, on the fourth day before the Kalends of June, in the sixth indiction, in the year 1188 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

### LX. He takes the Church of St. Nicholas of Stendal under protection and confirms its goods and privileges, on condition that one ounce of gold be paid annually to the Roman Church. (Lateran, 29 May.)

[RIEDEL, *Codex Diplomaticus Brandenburgensis*, I, vol. 5, p. 22.]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the provost of St. Nicholas at Stendal and his brethren, present and future, canonically appointed, forever.

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just requests. We receive the aforesaid Church of St. Nicholas of Stendal, in which you are devoted to divine service, into the right and property of blessed Peter and under the protection of the Apostolic See, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods your said church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or by other lawful means, with the Lord’s assistance, shall remain firm and undiminished to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The place itself in which the aforesaid church stands, with all its appurtenances; the village of Garlippe, with all that belongs to it; all the churches situated in Stendal; two talents from building-plots and three talents from the merchants’ house in the same castle; the church of Scinne; the mill of Rokenzhe.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, ordinations of clerics who are to be promoted to holy orders, and the other ecclesiastical sacraments from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to provide these things to you freely and without any improper exaction. Otherwise, you may have recourse to whatever bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested.

Moreover, by this present writing we decree that you shall receive the care of souls not from the archdeacon but from the diocesan bishop, if he judges it right to entrust it to you; otherwise, you shall hold it by apostolic commission.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no one at all to rashly disturb the aforesaid church, remove its possessions, retain those removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See. Further, as a sign that this church belongs in a special manner to blessed Peter, and of the liberty received from the Apostolic See, you shall pay one ounce of gold annually to us and to our successors. If therefore in future, etc.

Given at the Lateran, by the hand of Brother Moses, subdeacon of the holy Roman Church, acting vice-chancellor, on the fourth day before the Kalends of June [29 May], in the sixth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1188, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

### LXI. He affirms for the canons of the Church of St. Peter at Rome the privilege granted by Eugenius III.  
[Note: [Col. 1353] See *Patrologia*, vol. CLXXX, year 1153, 10 April, no. 577.] (Lateran, 2 June.)

[Bullar. Vatic., I, 72.]

[Col. 1353A]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of the basilica of the Prince of the Apostles, and the rectors of the four monasteries of Saints John and Paul, St. Martin, St. Stephen Major, and St. Stephen Minor, present and future, canonically appointed, forever.

The fellowship of blessed Peter and Paul is so eminent and glorious that both are teachers of the nations, authors of martyrs, and princes of priests. Although they surpass all the apostles by a certain special prerogative, they do not experience inequality, their merits in heaven being equal. To Peter the keys of the kingdom of heaven were entrusted by our Savior himself, the Lord Jesus Christ; Paul was chosen by God so that through his preaching he might fill the kingdom of heaven from the multitude of the nations. Peter is the rock and foundation of faith, and supports us firmly in solidity lest we fall; Paul, lest we be wounded by the perverse teaching of heretics, arms us with moral integrity and with the invincible reasoning of faith. Peter, holding primacy, binds and looses by his authority; Paul, a loving preacher, wonderfully strengthens us by exhortation, lest anything blameworthy or deserving of binding appear in us. Peter is our support and the house of strength; planted and rooted in his faith, we stand. Paul, the vessel of election, summoned with the sound of the heavenly trumpet those predestined and chosen by God; and, praying unceasingly for us, he protects us by interceding with God, lest we depart from faith and truth.

Since, therefore, these two great lights, illuminating God’s Church with equal and friendly splendor and shining forth in brotherly love, the principle of equity and justice persuades us—who, though unworthy, exercise Christ’s office on earth and are seen to sit in the chair of the Prince of the Apostles himself—to love the household of blessed Peter with paternal affection and to assist it with pious provision in its necessities. Moved, therefore, by the obligation of this consideration, beloved sons in the Lord, after the example of Pope Eugenius, our predecessor of happy memory, with the consent of our brother bishops and cardinals, we grant you by apostolic authority and confirm by this present writing one fourth of all offerings which accrue from the altar of the same blessed Apostle Peter, both from the chest and from all the ministries of the church, except the ministry of blessed Leo. This is granted on the condition that, whenever you wish, you shall have free power to retain and keep that offering in your own hands, or, with the consent of us and our successors, to sell it to whomsoever you choose; while in all other matters the free administration and custody of that church remains reserved in the hands of us and our successors.

We have judged it fitting to do this so that you, laboring zealously day and night in the praises of God—in the celebration of Masses, at matins, and at the other hours, diligently and fittingly sung for the salvation of the living and the dead—may honor the aforesaid Church of blessed Peter with due service; and so that God’s faithful, visiting the thresholds of the Apostles with fitting devotion, may always hold that place in greater devotion and reverence.

We therefore decree that no person whatever may, by rash presumption, violate or in any way disturb the text of this our grant. [Col. 1354B] If in future any ecclesiastical or secular person should presume to attempt this, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not correct that presumption by fitting satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor; let such a person know himself or herself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let that person be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance.

But upon all who preserve this our ordinance for that place may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and hereafter find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

[Col. 1354C] I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of St. Mark. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of St. Mary across the Tiber, title of St. Callistus. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Melior, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, title of Pammachius. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St. Cecilia. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St. Clement. I, Bobo, cardinal priest of the title of St. Anastasia. I, Alexius, cardinal priest of the title of St. Susanna. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St. Peter in Chains. [Col. 1354D] I, Jordan, cardinal priest of St. Pudentiana, title of Pastor. I, James, deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of the title of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Geoffrey, cardinal deacon of the title of St. Mary in Via Lata. I, Bobo, cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Portico. [Col. 1355A] I, John Felix, cardinal deacon of St. Eustace beside the temple of Agrippa. I, John, cardinal deacon of St. Theodore. I, Bernard, cardinal deacon of St. Mary the New. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Aquino.

Given at the Lateran, by the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the holy Roman Church, acting vice-chancellor, on the fourth day before the Nones of June [2 June], in the sixth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1188, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

### LXII. Privilege for the monastery of St. Gilbert of Nine Springs, diocese of Clermont. (Lateran, 3 June.)

[LABBE, *Nova Bibliotheca Manuscriptorum*, II, 752.]

[Col. 1355B] CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons JOHN, abbot of the Church of Blessed Gilbert of Nine Springs, and his brethren, present and future, professing the religious life.

It is fitting that we should willingly assent to the vows of religious persons which accord with reason and propriety, and bring them to effective completion, so that they may adhere to the Roman Church with more fervent devotion when they see that their just petitions have been heard more diligently and effectively. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your reasonable petition and receive the aforesaid Church, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, after the example of Pope Lucius, our predecessor of happy memory; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order which is known to have been established in that place according to God, the Rule of blessed Augustine, and the institution of the brethren of Prémontré, shall there be observed inviolate for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, with the Lord’s assistance, shall remain firm and undiminished to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The place itself in which the church stands, with all its appurtenances; the land of Insula; the wood and land of Monte Cesant; and the land from Robe as far as Andalo, which Hugh of Castellione gave to that church; also the fiefs of the whole lordship of Schola, which you may lawfully acquire, as the aforesaid Hugh and his sons lawfully granted them to you; the wood and land of Born; the wood of Bruvenc; the tithe of Aubin; the grange of Bostat; the grange and wood of Agilaret, with their appurtenances; the grange and wood of Bornat, with their appurtenances; the grange of Scholula, with its appurtenances; the grange of Edumarius, with its appurtenances; the grange of Vercilloliis; the grange of Rozeria; the grange of Montecanino and Cotors; the Church of St. John of Monteladerio; the chapel of the sisters of Schola; the mill of Vante [Col. 1356A] and the meadows; the Church of Lezach; the tithe from the land of Eschances; the mill of Buifferia; the annual rents which you possess in the castellany of Montispancier; the land of Mazeriae; the tithe which you possess in the vineyards of the castle of Schola; and the tithe of St. Remigius.

No one shall presume to exact tithes from you on the fruits of your labor which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the increase of your animals. You may also receive clerics and laypeople fleeing from the world, free and absolved, for conversion, and retain them without any contradiction. Furthermore, we forbid any of your brethren, after making profession in that place, to leave it without his abbot’s permission; and no one may dare retain a departing brother unless he has the certificate of the community’s letters.

When a general interdict is imposed upon the land, you may celebrate divine offices in a low voice behind closed doors, excluding those excommunicated and under interdict. We also forbid any church, land, or benefice bestowed upon your church to be given personally to anyone or alienated in any manner without the consent of the whole chapter, or of its greater and sounder part. If any gifts or alienations are made otherwise than has been stated, we decree them void.

Moreover, no canons or conversi bound by profession in your house may stand surety for anyone or receive money on loan from anyone, without the consent of the abbot and the greater part of your chapter, beyond the amount established by the provision of your chapter, unless this is for the manifest benefit of your house. If they presume to do so, the community shall in no way be bound to answer for them.

Further, in your causes you may produce brethren fit to testify, and by their testimony, as justice requires, repel injury and vindicate right. To avoid the frequented resort of secular persons, you may, without prejudice to the right of the diocesan bishop and parish church, build oratories on your granges and, when necessary, celebrate divine offices in them for yourselves alone and your household.

For chrism, holy oil, consecrations of churches, ordinations of clerics to be promoted to holy [Col. 1356D] orders, the bringing of an abbot to his seat, or any other sacraments, no one may dare demand anything from you, whether under pretext of custom or in any other way. Since tithes are known, under both the Old and New Law, to have been granted by laypeople to the ministers of the Church, we forbid, under threat of anathema, that you be harassed by exactions of tithes.

We also decree that the burial-place of that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have chosen to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; the right of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken being nevertheless preserved.

Desiring also to provide with paternal care for your peace and tranquility, we forbid by apostolic authority that within the enclosures of your sites or granges anyone should commit robbery or theft, set fire, seize or kill a person, or dare exercise any violence. On the death of you, the abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any trickery, deceit, or violence, save the person whom the brethren, by common consent or by the greater part of the sounder counsel, shall provide to be elected according to God and the Rule of blessed Augustine.

We therefore decree that no person whatever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, remove its possessions, retain those removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole and undiminished for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If therefore in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Belligensis. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of St. Mark. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of St. Mary across the Tiber, title of St. Callistus. I, Melior, cardinal priest of Saints John, Paul, and Pammachius. [Col. 1357C] I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St. Cecilia. I, Ralph, cardinal priest of the title of St. Praxedes. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St. Clement. I, James, cardinal deacon of St. Mary. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saints George and Bacchus. I, Baro, cardinal deacon of St. George. I, John, cardinal deacon of St. Theodore.

Given at the Lateran, by the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the holy Roman Church, acting vice-chancellor, on the third day before the Nones of June [3 June], [Col. 1357D] in the sixth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1188, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

Sealed with a lead seal upon a silken cord.

### LXIII. He urges Joachim, abbot of Curatio, to “complete the *Exposition of the Apocalypse* and the work of *Concord*, and to strive diligently to correct them.” (Lateran, 8 June.)

[MANRIQUE, *Annals of the Cistercians*, III, 211.]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son JOACHIM, abbot of Curatio, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The order of reason advises, and the duty of charity demands, that in all our acts we should strive most earnestly for this: that, according to the testimony of evangelical truth, our works may shine before human beings, so that they may take from them material and an example for improvement. Since, therefore, at the command and exhortation of Pope Lucius, our predecessor of good memory, you are said to have begun an exposition of the Apocalypse and a work of concord, and afterward, by the authority of Pope Urban, his successor, to have composed them, we admonish and exhort your charity in the Lord, commanding by apostolic writings that, bringing your labors in this matter to their desired and due conclusion, with God’s grace attending, you complete that work for the benefit of your neighbors and diligently endeavor to correct it; so that, when you come to us as soon as opportunity permits, you may present yourself and it to the examination and judgment of the Apostolic See. [Col. 1358B] For if you wish to retain it in secret, take diligent care that you may be able to appease, by fitting satisfaction, the offense of the supreme householder concerning the talent of learning entrusted to you.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Ides of June [8 June], in the first year of our pontificate.

### LXIV. He takes the Church of St. Mary of Viborg under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. (Lateran, 8 June.)

[THORKELIN, *Diplomata Arna-Magnaeana*, I, 61.]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons TUCHO, provost of the Church of St. Mary of Viborg, and his brethren, present and future, professing the religious life, forever.

A petition of pious purpose ought to be followed by effective fulfillment, so that the sincerity of devotion may be worthily made known and the requested benefit may undoubtedly obtain force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and, following the footsteps of our predecessors of pious memory, Innocent and Alexander, Roman pontiffs, we receive the aforesaid Church of St. Mary, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree that the canonical order which is known to have been instituted in the same church according to God and the Rule of blessed Augustine shall be observed there inviolate for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, with the Lord’s assistance, shall remain firm and undiminished to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The Church of Blessed Margaret the Virgin, which our venerable brother Nicholas, your bishop, as we have learned from his letters, resigned to you. We also confirm by apostolic authority to your devotion the Church of Blessed Martin which is on the island of Fur, so that henceforth both of them shall remain under your administration and disposal.

Concerning also the Lenten provisions which the bishop at one time had in your church, and on account of which contentions used seriously to trouble your religious community, we decree that, just as the bishop already mentioned is known to have resigned and remitted them to you for the future by his privilege on equitable consideration, so this shall henceforth be maintained: neither he nor his successor may at any time require provisions from you contrary to this. We further forbid the bishop to receive from the offerings brought to the bodies of saints in your church anything beyond the fourth part which he was accustomed to receive.

Moreover, by the tenor of this document we grant that no one may unjustly presume to invade the estates or possessions of your church, whether situated within or outside your city, contrary to your administration. In the election of your bishop you shall have the first voice, since you are canons of the cathedral church, as is known to belong to you by the law of the canons and by ancient custom observed down to these times. Nor shall anyone from elsewhere be elected your bishop so long as, according to the statutes of the canons, there is found in your church—which is the cathedral—one qualified person who can be chosen by canonical and unanimous consent without any impropriety.

No one whatever may dare alter for the worse the cloister customs which are known to have been commendably maintained hitherto in your place; rather, they shall always remain unshaken in their force. Further, we decree that no prince may remove anyone from the cloister without the consent of the provost and brethren.

No one shall presume to demand or exact tithes from you on your newly cleared lands which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the increase of your animals. We also grant that the burial-place of that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who choose to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken being nevertheless preserved. On the death of you, the present provost of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by the cunning of trickery or by violence, save the person whom the brethren, by common consent or by the greater part of the sounder counsel, shall provide to be elected according to God and the Rule of blessed Augustine.

We therefore decree that no person whatever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, remove its possessions, retain those removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of your bishop.

If in future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this text of our constitution, [Col. 1360A] and, having been warned a second or third time, does not correct the offense by fitting satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor; let such a person know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and let that person be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance.

But upon all who preserve their rights for that place may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. [Col. 1360B] I, John, cardinal priest of the title of St. Mark. I, Laborans, bishop and cardinal priest of St. Mary across the Tiber, title of St. Callistus. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Melior, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, title of Gamael. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St. Cecilia. I, Radulf, cardinal priest of the title of St. Praxedes. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St. Clement. [Col. 1360C] I, Bobo, cardinal priest of the title of St. Anastasia. I, Alexius, cardinal priest of the title of St. Susanna. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St. Peter in Chains. I, Jordan, cardinal priest of St. Pudentiana, title of Pastor. I, James, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, John, cardinal deacon of St. Theodore. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. [Col. 1360D] I, Bernard, cardinal deacon of St. Mary the New.

Given at the Lateran, by the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the holy Roman Church, acting vice-chancellor, on the sixth day before the Ides of June [8 June], in the sixth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1188, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

### LXV. He permits Absalon, archbishop of Lund, to enroll Ketil, formerly provost of St. Mary of Viborg, among the saints. (Lateran, 9 June.)

[LANGEBEK, *Writers of Danish Affairs*, IV, 432.]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother in Christ ABSALON, archbishop of Lund, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has come to the hearing of our apostolic office through the letters of you, our venerable brother, and of our beloved son in Christ, Canute, king of the Danes, together with the representation of the suffragan bishops, that Ketil, of good memory, a religious man and provost of the Church of St. Mary of Viborg, shone among you with many virtues while he lived. After his death, God, wondrous in his saints, continually works many miracles through his merits, so that the signs of miracles after his departure declare without any ambiguity what manner of life he had lived.

Although it has been suggested to us that we should cause the memory of the aforesaid Ketil to be celebrated in the catalogue of saints, nevertheless, because the truth of this matter has not been fully established, we command you by apostolic writing to summon your suffragans and religious men—especially those who are said to have known his life and conduct—and, with their testimony and affirmation, to investigate with vigilant care his deeds and the miracles by which he is said to shine after death. If it appears fitting and proper to you, canonize his memory and decree by apostolic authority that his observance be held in future ages as that of a holy man.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Ides of June [9 June], in the first year of our pontificate.

### LXVI. He approves a judgment rendered by Bishop Gerard and Archdeacon Vitalian of Padua between Mark, bishop of Castello (Venice), and the parish priests and priests of certain churches concerning certain tithes. He confirms the possessions of the Church of St. Canziano. (Lateran, 9 June.)

[HORMAYR, *History of the Entire County of Tyrol*, I, II, 121.]

[Col. 1361C]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PEREGRINUS, parish priest of the Church of St. Canziano, and his brethren and successors canonically appointed, forever.

It is equitable and consonant with reason that we should settle by means of justice disputes brought before the hearing of our apostolic office, and that things assigned to the benefit of churches either by judgment or by any just title should be so established by apostolic authority that they cannot in future be disturbed by the malice of anyone. For judgments would seem to be rendered to no purpose if anyone were allowed to violate them at will and they were repeatedly called into doubt, unless they were strengthened by the protection of written documents. When disputes have been settled by judgment or agreement, and judgments have been reduced to writing, if any doubt later arises and is quieted by the authority of a superior, so that it may not relapse into the difficulty of dispute, it is fitting that the conclusion imposed be strengthened by the protection of a written instrument.

Since, therefore, a controversy was formerly debated between you and the parish priests and priests of certain other churches on the one side, and our venerable brother Mark, bishop of Castello, on the other, concerning certain portions of tithes; and since our venerable brother Gerard, bishop, and our beloved son Vitalian, archdeacon and canon of Padua, by command of Urban and Gregory, Roman pontiffs of happy memory, our predecessors, settled it by their judgment; and since afterward Philip of Lupriolo, parish priest of the Church of St. Luke, and John of Lanza, priest of the Church of St. Cassian, your procurators, together with Michael of St. Angelo, procurator of the bishop of Castello himself, and of the canons of the Church of Castello and the clerics of the other churches who sought to invalidate that judgment, appeared in our presence: by our command, before the examination of our beloved son Soffred, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Via Lata, arguments were put forward on either side regarding the questions which had arisen.

By the common counsel of our brethren, we have judged that same judgment to be confirmed by apostolic authority and strengthened by the protection of our letters. For greater security, we have ordered the text of the instrument containing that judgment to be inserted word for word.

In the name of the eternal God, in the year of His Nativity 1188, in the sixth indiction, on the fourteenth day of January, in the presence of those whose names will be stated below, concerning the case pending between Mark, bishop of Castello, and the parish priests and priests of Venice, the lord Vitalian, canon and delegated archdeacon of Padua, together with Lord Gerard, bishop of Padua by God’s grace, delegated by Lord Pope Urban, with the consent of the aforesaid bishop, who was present and consenting, for himself and for that bishop, recited the following judgment:

In the name of the Lord: We, Gerard, by God’s grace bishop of Padua, and Vitalian, canon of Padua and delegated archdeacon, appointed by Lord Urban of good memory concerning the case pending between the venerable Mark, bishop of the Church of Castello, on the one side, and the parish priests and priests of St. Canziano, St. Sophia, St. Mary Mother of the Lord, St. Paul, St. Luke, St. Jeremiah, St. Hermagoras, St. Baudi, St. Margaret, St. Simeon the Prophet, and St. Gervasius, on the other, concerning certain portions of tithes—with the archpriest of Padua, who had been assigned to us by that same pope as an associate for hearing the matter, removed, and the abbot of Carario appointed in his place; and finally, the aforesaid abbot having been excluded from the said hearing by Lord Pope Gregory of happy memory—Leonard, primicerius, acting as procurator for the bishop of Castello, and Dominic, first archdeacon, acting as procurator for the aforesaid parish priests and priests, having appeared in this case: the case was thus begun and debated before us.

The archdeacon, on behalf of those whose procurator he was, demanded from the aforesaid procurator of the bishop that the lord bishop should allow the parish priests and priests of the aforesaid churches to possess whole and entire the fourth part of the tithes due to the clerics. This was to be so, however, that the clerics of each individual church should have the principal right, and among themselves should divide that fourth part which arose from the tithes of their own parishioners. He also demanded that the same bishop should leave to them in full the fourth part due to the poor and the part due to the repair of the churches, retaining no fourth part of either for himself.

In reply, the bishop’s procurator said that they ought not to possess entire the fourth part due to the clerics; rather, it ought to be distributed among all clerics according to the bishop’s disposition, as had been customary. He could lawfully retain one fourth of the fourth part due to the poor, both by consent of the clerics and because the care of the poor pertained especially to him; moreover, he justly held one fourth of the fourth part due to church fabric for the restoration of the mother church.

Therefore, having heard the matter concerning the aforesaid claims after setting aside the impediment of appeal, and having heard and examined the reasons, attestations, and allegations of both parties with care, and also having taken the advice of certain learned clerics, we pronounce that the aforesaid parish priests and priests shall have whole and entire, as their principal right, the fourth part assigned to the clerics which proceeds from their parishioners; and that the clerics of each of the aforesaid churches shall divide among themselves the fourth part which arises from the tithes of their parishioners. We condemn the aforesaid Leonard, procurator, and the bishop, to permit them peacefully to possess and divide it in this manner.

We absolve the aforesaid Leonard, procurator, and the bishop himself from the claim to the fourth part which the bishop was accustomed to retain from the fourth part due to the poor, and from the claim to the other fourth part which he retained, from the fourth part due to church fabric, for the restoration of the mother church—the claim made by the aforesaid archdeacon and procurator on behalf of the often-mentioned parish priests and priests. And, that these acts may be believed more certainly to have been performed by us, we have caused this judgment to be marked with our own seals.

Given in the episcopal chamber at Padua. Witnesses: Adam, Almeric, Cerutus, Tamboanus, Theotonicellus, Ugolino, canons of Padua; Priest Paul of the Church of St. Andrew; the master, the little bishop of St. Martin; Michael, priest and parish priest of St. Angelo of Venice; Rainald, cleric of that same church; Gufredinus, cleric of St. Lucy; Gnafus; and many others.

I, Boninus, notary of Lord Emperor Frederick, was present and wrote this judgment at the command of the aforesaid lord bishop and Vitalian, canon and archdeacon of Padua.

Because, however, from the fourth part assigned for the repair of the church [Col. 1363C], the aforesaid bishop permanently reserved one quarter for himself and his successors for the benefit of the mother church, and decreed that the other parts of that same fourth should be conferred upon you and your successors, under the common privilege granted to parish priests, priests, and clerics of other churches, for repairing the fabric of your church, its books, and other necessities; and because, from the fourth assigned to the poor, as plainly appears from the tenor of the privilege of the same bishop, that bishop decreed that three parts should be distributed to the poor of your parish, reserving the fourth for himself during his lifetime: we confirm by the page of this present writing that concession, as canonically made by the same bishop and confirmed by an authentic document. Moreover, we grant you and your successors full authority to make out instruments of security [Col. 1363D] for your parishioners from whom you have received tithes. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods the aforesaid church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the grant of pontiffs, the liberality of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by the Lord’s favor, acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: the site itself on which the aforesaid church stands, with all its appurtenances, lands, paths, and everything else belonging to that church.

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for absolutely no person to rashly disturb the aforesaid church, or take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations whatsoever; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and to the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second and third time, should fail to correct the offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of office and honor, and recognize himself or herself guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let that person be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer, and be subject at the final judgment to strict vengeance [Col. 1364B].

But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen. Amen. Amen.

I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, have subscribed. I, John, priest-cardinal, at that time of Saint Mark, have subscribed. I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of Saint Mary beyond the Tiber, at that time of Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Pandulf, priest-cardinal of Saints John [Col. 1364C] and Paul, at that time of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, Peter, priest-cardinal, at that time of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Radulf, priest-cardinal of the church of Praxedes, have subscribed. I, James, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Gratian, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Octavian, deacon-cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Soffredus, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Gregory, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, John Felix, deacon-cardinal of Saint Eustace [Col. 1364D] beside the temple of Agrippa, have subscribed. I, John, deacon-cardinal of Saint Theodore, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church and acting chancellor, on the fifth day before the Ides of June, in the sixth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1188, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

### LXVII. He confirms by apostolic authority to the priests and clerics of Saint Mary Mother of the Lord the portion of tithes granted to them by Mark Nicholas, bishop of Castello, and decrees that the goods of that church shall remain secure and unimpaired. (Lateran, 9 June.)

[F. CORNELIUS, *Venetian Churches*, vol. II, p. 305.]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the priests and clerics of the church of Saint Mary Mother of the Lord, present and future, canonically appointed in perpetuity.

It is equitable and consonant with reason that controversies brought before the hearing of our apostolate should be settled through justice, etc., as in the preceding letter.

I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Mark. I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of Saint Mary beyond the Tiber, title of Calixtus. I, Pandulf, priest-cardinal of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles [Col. 1365B]. I, Melior, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul, title of Pammachius. I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Rodulf, cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, James, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary, title of Cosmedin. I, Gratian, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Octavian, deacon-cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Siffredus, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Via Lata [Col. 1365C]. I, Gregory, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Portico. I, John Felix, deacon-cardinal of Saint Eustace beside the temple of Agrippa.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church, acting in place of the chancellor, on the fifth day before the Ides of June, in the sixth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1188, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

I, Donatus, priest and notary of Saint Mary Mother of the Lord, copied this copy from the authentic document of Lord Pope Clement III, sealed with his lead seal. In the year of the Lord 1200, on the twenty-eighth day of November, in the second indiction, at Rialto, adding or omitting nothing that would alter the tenor, I wrote, completed, and authenticated it [Col. 1365D].

### LXVIII. He receives the church of Saint Cassian of Venice under Saint Peter’s protection and confirms its rights and revenues by apostolic authority. (Lateran, 9 June.)

[Ibid., p. 399.]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons DOMINIC PINO, parish priest of Saint Cassian, and his procurators, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

A pious request ought to be fulfilled by an effect corresponding to the will, so that both the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the requested benefit may undoubtedly acquire force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive the aforesaid church of Saint Cassian, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves; and we strengthen it with the protection of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions or goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, through grants of pontiffs, the liberality of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by the Lord’s favor, acquire, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The site itself on which the aforesaid church stands, with all its appurtenances, lands, and paths [Col. 1366B] belonging to that church.
