Hence we are not without cause astonished that, as is alleged, after an appeal had been made to the Apostolic See and after the prohibition of Urban, our predecessor of good memory, you have so increased your actions concerning the construction of the new chapel and many other matters to the harm of the brethren of the church entrusted to you that it may be judged that no benefit from the remedy of the appeal entered has accrued to them, as the legal rule requires, nor that you have shown the honour due to the most holy Roman Church, your mother. Although it is our purpose to show your brotherhood as much deference as we can in God, and to honour your person in all things incumbent on us by virtue of our office, nevertheless we neither can nor ought to pass over with closed eyes the oppressions and cries of those brethren, consistently with a good conscience. Therefore, with the counsel of our brethren, by apostolic letters we command and strictly prescribe to your brotherhood that, setting aside every contradiction and excuse—even if it happens that you are absent [Col. 1420A] from your church—you shall not delay to demolish whatever has been done in constructing the chapel after the appeal to the Apostolic See or the prohibition of our predecessor; you shall revoke and wholly nullify whatever has been done and wrongly innovated concerning the appointment of canons and other matters connected with the chapel. You shall also keep excluded from office and benefice those who, after the prohibition of our often-mentioned predecessor, presumed to celebrate divine offices in that chapel, until they make suitable satisfaction to us. You shall restore the ministers of the convent whom you removed after the appeal had been entered and whom that same predecessor restored; and you shall likewise hold absolved those whom, after the appeal had been entered, you sought to excommunicate or suspend. You shall restore to their former condition, all appeal and contradiction being set aside, all things undertaken after that appeal to their detriment: namely, the seizure of their villages and possessions, their revenues, and other things which they had before the appeal, and likewise the taking away of other property.

Further, because according to the rule of law nothing is to be innovated after an appeal, we will and command that, while judgment is pending, you make no effort whatsoever to alter anything concerning the state of the monastery to the detriment of those brethren. We additionally command under precept that you shall not delay, within forty days after receiving these letters, to restore to those monks everything which, after the appeal or previously, you unlawfully took from them without due process of law—namely, gifts, churches, villages, possessions, [Col. 1420C] revenues, or other things—together with a suitable compensation for the fruits subsequently and unlawfully received, and together with their proper and free liberties and administration.

We also command those monks under precept that, if they have presumed anything against your right and honour, they shall make suitable satisfaction to you, appeal set aside. Since the prior of that monastery died while pursuing this case, we will and command under precept that you shall not proceed with the appointment of a prior contrary to the privileges of the Apostolic See, the Rule of St Benedict, and the reasonable custom hitherto observed in the monastery; and if you do so, appeal set aside, you shall not delay to revoke it, notwithstanding any letters procured from the Apostolic See to the prejudice of their right. Otherwise, we have instructed our beloved son John, cardinal priest of the title of St Mark, legate of the Apostolic See, that by apostolic authority he shall compel you, all objectors, and the monks themselves, should they prove rebellious, to these measures by ecclesiastical coercion, all obstacle of appeal being removed; and that he shall likewise not delay to compel, by similar censure, those whom he knows have been named for a fuller investigation of the truth, to bear testimony to the truth, setting aside favour and fear.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth Ides of March, in the second year of our pontificate.

### CX. He receives the Monastery of Muri under the protection of St Peter, confirms all privileges also granted by Pope Alexander, and adds new ones.  
*(Lateran, 13 March.)*

[HERGOTT, *Genealogia diplomatica gentis Habsburgicæ*, II, 202.]

[Col. 1421A]

Clement, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Anselm, abbot of the monastery of St Martin at Muri, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

For those who, laying aside worldly desires, have vowed in the habit of religion to render the service owed to the Lord, apostolic support ought to be more readily available, lest the assault of any rash person should either call them back from their purpose or—God forbid—break the strength of religion [Col. 1421B]. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and, after the example of Pope Alexander, our predecessor of blessed memory, fortify by the privilege of the present writing, the aforesaid monastery in which you are dedicated to divine service. First, indeed, we decree that the monastic order known to have been established in that monastery according to God and the Rule of St Benedict shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may in the future acquire by grants of pontiffs, generosity [Col. 1421C] of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have considered it proper to state the following by their own names:

The church of Buoches; the church of Stannes; the church of Gersowo; the church of Riske; the church of Chussennacho; the church of Agetiswilare; the church of Telleuwilare; the church of Rordorf; the church of Egenwilare; the church of Stallenchon; the church of Gorelinchon; the church of Urtinchon; a fifth part of the tithes in the church of Stallenchon; a twelfth part of the tithes in the church of Reinfriswile; a twentieth part of the tithes in the church of Surse; the estate of Gersogo with its appurtenances; the estate of Spreitenbach, from which seven goatskins are rendered to you [Col. 1421D]; the estate of Buoches with its appurtenances; the estate of Chussennacho with its appurtenances; the estate of Gangolfeswile; the estate of Trespach. In Waltrat, nine holdings; the estate of Alinchon with its appurtenances; the estate of Vicwile with its appurtenances; the estate of Cunentvellum; the estate of Gopenowo with its appurtenances; the estate of Chalpac; the estate of Wilperc; the estate of Cholumbrowo; the estate of Columhare; the estate of Chutingen; the estate of Tintinkon; the estate of Hechilingen; the estate of Totinkon; the estate of Tulleheim; the estate of Rainfriswile; the estate of Rotwile with its appurtenances; the estate of Bellenchon with its appurtenances; the estate of Urdorf; the estate of Spreitenbach; the estate of Tellinchon; the estate of Winchele; the estate of Escherwile; [Col. 1422A] the estate of Boranwile; the estate of Holunstraze; the estate of Tegerano; the estate of Otwizingen; the estate of Hagenbuochon; the estate of Ratolfesperc; the estate of Winteswille; the estate of Lennes; the estate of Renferswile; the estate of Boswile with its appurtenances; the estate of Ruti; the estate of Woloswile; the estate of Maswandom; the estate of Gamelinchon; the estate of Pensiwile; the estate of Ipinchon; the estate of Selenburon; the estate of Tennenwile; the estate of Schinsenacho; the estate of Bozeberch; the estate of Sizinchon; the parish church with its three chapels, Hermoteswile, Pozwilo, and Wolon. Since the aforesaid church and chapels have reasonably been assigned for your food and clothing, we grant that you shall possess them at present, and confirm this by apostolic authority.

Moreover, by the authority of this present document [Col. 1422B] we grant that, if your advocate, exceeding the rights of advocacy, imposes unlawful exactions upon you, your monastery, or its belongings, and otherwise proves burdensome and useless to you, then, unless after admonition he reforms, you may choose another advocate, of greater age, from the castle of Abespurc, through whom the rights of the monastery may be better and unimpairedly defended against the plunder and violence of wrongdoers. Nor may that advocate in any way dare to grant anything belonging to the monastery—whether lands, serfs, or the advocacy itself—to anyone.

We further decree that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last wish [Col. 1422C] of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; yet the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken are preserved. When, however, a general interdict of the land is in force, you may celebrate the divine offices behind closed doors, without ringing bells, excluding excommunicated persons and those under interdict, and in a subdued voice. Upon the death of the present abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one may be appointed there through any deceitful stratagem or force, except one whom the brethren, by common consent or by the sounder part of their counsel, shall determine ought to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery [Col. 1422D], take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but all things shall remain whole and unimpaired, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and, in your parish churches, the canonical right of the diocesan bishops. As a token of this protection received from the Apostolic See, you shall pay one gold coin each year to us and our successors.

If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1423A] I, John, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Albert, cardinal-priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Alexius, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, James, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Gratian, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Gerard, cardinal-deacon of Saint Adrian.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church, acting as vice-chancellor, on the third Ides of March, in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1188. [Note: [Col. 1423D] Substitute the year 1189; the chronology then agrees.] In the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

## CXI. He takes the monastery of Saint Mary of Esrum under protection, and confirms its possessions and privileges.  
*(Lateran, 16 March.)*

[THORKELIN, *Diplom. Arna-Magn.*, I, 277.]

[Col. 1423B]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot of Saint Mary of Esrum and his brethren, present and future, who profess the regular life: in perpetuity.

It is fitting that those choosing the religious life should receive apostolic protection, lest perhaps the assault of any rash person either turn them from their purpose or, which God forbid, weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and we take under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery [Col. 1423C] of Saint Mary of Esrum, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present document.

First, we decree that the monastic order which is known to have been instituted there according to God, the Rule of blessed Benedict, and the institution of the Cistercian brethren shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, through the grants of popes, the gifts of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, God granting it, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names [Col. 1423D]:

The site itself upon which the aforesaid monastery stands, with all its adjacent lands and appurtenances; the cloister itself of Hesram, with woods, meadows, mills, fisheries, and all its appurtenances; Widlingruth, Hafreholm, Byrgisholm, Sande, Fumathorp, Stenholt; the houses of Saint Martin, Hiarnetorp, Cracadal, Mothorp in Halland, and Glumsiensivig, with their villages, meadows, woods, and other appurtenances.

Certainly, from the produce of your labours, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or from the sustenance of your [Col. 1424A] animals, no one may presume to demand or extort tithes from you. You may also receive into conversion clerics or laymen fleeing from the world, free and absolved, and retain them without any opposition. Moreover, we forbid any of your brethren, after making profession in that place, to depart without the permission of his abbot; and no one may dare retain one who has departed, whether under protection of letters of common form or otherwise.

Desiring, further, with paternal concern to provide in future for your peace and tranquillity, we prohibit by apostolic authority anyone from daring, within the precincts of your places or granges, to commit theft or robbery, set fire, seize or kill a person, or commit any violence [Col. 1424B].

Moreover, by apostolic authority we decree that, as our predecessors have established, no bishop or other person may compel you to attend synods or secular courts. Nor may anyone, against your will, presume to visit your houses in order to celebrate ordinations, consecrate chrism, hear causes, or summon public assemblies. We also decree that, if the bishop in whose parish your house is founded should perhaps refuse, after being asked three times at intervals and with fitting humility, to bless a substitute abbot, [Note: [Col. 1423D] Supply: “you may approach whichever other bishop you wish [Col. 1424D], who, relying on our authority, may bless your own novices, etc.”] you may approach any other bishop whom you wish, who, relying on our authority, may bless your own novices and perform the other acts [Col. 1424C] belonging to his office, until that bishop reflects upon his obstinacy and does not refuse to bless the abbot who is to be blessed.

If bishops demand anything from you beyond the obedience due to them, or if the princes of the land demand something contrary to the liberty of the order granted you by our predecessors and ourselves, you shall be free by apostolic authority to refuse what is demanded, lest through this occasion the aforesaid order, hitherto free, be bound in the snare of human servitude. We further add that no bishop may impede the regular election of your abbot, or in any way interfere, contrary to the statutes of the Cistercian Order and the authority of your privileges, in appointing, removing, or deposing the person who holds office at the time. If bishops for this reason pronounce any sentence against [Col. 1424D] your churches or persons, we decree that sentence void, as having been issued contrary to grants of the Apostolic See.

When you cannot obtain the services of your own bishops, if a bishop passes through your district whom you know fully, you may receive from him—and from neighbouring bishops when the diocesan see is vacant—the blessings of vessels and vestments, the ordinations of monks, and the consecrations of altars; provided that no prejudice thereby be created in future against your own bishops.

By apostolic authority we also forbid [Col. 1425A] anyone to place under interdict, or bind with the bond of anathema, neighbouring or hired men because they have helped you with labour on days when you work and others keep holiday, under any pretext arising from the concessions bestowed upon you by apostolic generosity; or to proceed against your benefactors because, from their own property or through service, they have charitably given you some benefit. If anyone pronounces a sentence of excommunication or interdict against any member of your household, while that person remains in your service, on account of the withholding of tithes or of anything else granted by the Apostolic See to your order, you may absolve them in danger of death; and if their priests, when humbly requested, refuse or maliciously delay to do this, you may administer the ecclesiastical sacraments to them [Col. 1425B]. You may likewise pronounce, by our authority, a regular sentence against your monks or lay brothers who have left your cloister without their abbot’s permission, should anyone presume, against your will, to retain them.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular [Col. 1425C] person, etc.

I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, John, cardinal-priest of Saint Mary. I, Pandulf, cardinal-priest of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Albrand, cardinal-priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Bobo, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Alexander, cardinal-priest of the title of . . . I, Peter, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso. I, James, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Gratian, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Gerard, cardinal-deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Bernard, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary the New. [Col. 1425D] I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Aquino.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church, acting as vice-chancellor, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of April, in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1188, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

## CXII. He grants the prior and brethren of Fonte Avellana authority to reform the condition of the monastery of Saint Victor.  
*(Lateran, 16 March.)*

[MITTARELLI, *Annals of the Camaldolese*, IV, appendix, p. 179.]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons . . . the prior and brethren of Fonte Avellana: greeting and apostolic blessing.

When requests are made of the Apostolic See which concern the honour of religion and look to the peace and advancement of churches, it is fitting that we grant them willingly and carry them into effect. Therefore, assenting to your requests, we grant by apostolic authority that you may, as is especially your concern, dispose of and regulate according to rule the monastery of Saint Victor with its appurtenances, which belongs to you and is greatly disordered both in temporal and spiritual matters, and which it is expedient to restore through your care to a better condition; saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. Let no one, therefore, etc. If anyone, etc.

Given at the Lateran, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of April, in the second year of our pontificate.

## CXIII. He informs Gerald, prior, and the brethren of Grandmont that he has given John, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Mark and legate of the Apostolic See, a mandate publicly to declare that Stephen, founder of the Order of Grandmont, has been enrolled among the saints.  
*(Lateran, 21 March.)*

[*Acta Sanctorum*, February, vol. III, p. 204.]

[Col. 1426B]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GERALD, prior, and the brethren of Grandmont: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our Redeemer willed that the most holy Roman Church should be the head and teacher of all, so that, through the guidance of divine grace, matters which the faithful must undertake everywhere may be ordered at its direction and command; errors corrected for the better; and recourse had to its counsel in doubtful matters. No one, however much he may boast of his merits, may alter what it has decreed. For if indiscriminate licence were perhaps given to everyone to undertake whatever occurred to him according to his own will, then an indiscriminate freedom, since purposes differ according to the diversity of persons, would sometimes suppress what ought to be commended, without the balancing judgment of justice, to the scandal of others, and would celebrate things less worthy with undeserved praise.

Accordingly, our predecessor Urban of happy memory, having heard of the religion and the commendable purity of life in which Stephen, of holy memory, founder of the Order of Grandmont, had shone, and of the many attestations of miracles by which almighty God had wished to make his merits known to the world, chose to entrust a full investigation of these matters to the legates whom he sent to those regions to conduct certain business of the Church. Thus, on the testimony of those legates and other men whose evidence was undoubtedly to be trusted, they might proceed deliberately to do what seemed fitting both for the advantage of the faithful and for the honour of the holy man himself, who until then had lain hidden like a jewel in a dunghill.

We too, having been fully informed concerning the life, merits, and way of life in which the aforesaid holy man is said to have flourished, and concerning the manifold miraculous signs by which divine mercy wished to distinguish him, both through the testimony of our dearest son Henry, illustrious king of the English, and of our venerable brethren William of Reims, cardinal-priest of Saint Sabina; Bartholomew, archbishop of Tours; Elias, archbishop of Bordeaux; and Seibrand, bishop of Limoges [Col. 1427A]; and of our beloved sons Bobard, then cardinal-deacon of Saint Angel, and Octavian, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, who exercised the office of legate in those regions, as well as of many other bishops—we have judged that the execution of this matter should be entrusted to the discretion of our beloved son John, cardinal-priest of Saint Mark, legate of the Apostolic See. By apostolic letters we direct him, upon coming to your place and assembling the bishops of the neighbouring districts and the other religious men, to announce that we have enrolled Stephen among the saints by the authority which we exercise; that he is henceforth to be reckoned in the catalogue of saints; and that, through his merits, the help of the Redeemer is to be sought together with the intercessions of the other saints [Col. 1427B].

Given at the Lateran, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of April, in the second year of our pontificate.

## CXIV. He takes the church of Saint Peter at Douai under protection and confirms its goods.  
*(Lateran, 31 March.)*

[MIRAEUS, *Diplomatic Works*, III, 356.]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the provost of the church of Saint Peter at Douai and his brethren, present and future, to be canonically appointed: for perpetual remembrance.

Both the strength [Col. 1427C] of equity and the order of reason require that just petitioners be granted their requests, especially when piety supports the petitioners’ will and truth does not abandon it. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests. Following the example of Pope Alexander, our predecessor of happy memory, we take the aforesaid church of Saint Peter at Douai, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and fortify it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, God granting it, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors [Col. 1427D]. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

From the gift of Robert, formerly bishop of Arras: the altar of Marcha Gotranni, for the use of the canons serving God there, with the rights of the bishop of Arras and his officials fully preserved. From the gift of the same man: the altar of Saint Rictrudis of Wasiers, with its endowments, for the use of the same canons, free and unencumbered exactly as he granted it to you; with all revenues of the bishop and the customs of the archdeacon and his officials preserved. Upon the death or lawful removal of the priest of that place, it shall belong to your community to provide another suitable priest and present him to the bishop of Arras, to whom he shall promise obedience.

[Col. 1428A] All tithes of your parish and all offerings which Gerard, formerly bishop of Cambrai, granted for the use of the canons of your church, while the bishoprics of Cambrai and Arras were still united; upon the condition, namely, that no lay person shall ever govern your church or its property, but that it shall be administered only by a provost who is a cleric, taking charge of granting prebends and ordering the other affairs of the church. We have also willed that it remain free and absolved from all provisions-in-kind and every fiscal obligation, as that bishop decreed; yet the right of the bishop of Arras is preserved, as in other abbeys.

From the gift of the said Robert, formerly bishop of Arras: the altars and churches of Saint Martin of Sin [Col. 1428B] and Saint Remigius of Marcha, with their endowments and appurtenances, for the use of the canons serving God there; all venality and exaction of shameful profit having been removed by that bishop. You shall possess them freely, by perpetual right, exactly as he lawfully granted them to you, with all episcopal cathedral revenues and the customs of the archdeacon preserved.

Upon the death or lawful removal of a priest in any of the aforesaid places, you shall present another suitable priest to the bishop of Arras; he shall promise obedience to the bishop and shall then receive gratis from the bishop’s hand the pastoral care to be exercised among the people. Nevertheless, some of you shall endeavour to attend the synod of Arras every year, unless they are excused by the bishop’s favour. The two chapels of Blessed Mary, one in the suburb of Douai and the other outside the suburb, which Dulcetus caused to be made free and unencumbered, shall remain as your church has hitherto lawfully been known to possess them. Upon the death or lawful removal of the priest of that place, you shall provide another suitable priest there.

No assent of any laymen, contrary to the custom of the church itself, shall be accepted concerning the alteration of prebends established in your church out of the goods of Provost Robert, Simon, and Gerard. The chapel of Saint Nicholas in the parish of Sin, and the other chapel of Saint Nicholas situated in the parish of Saint Peter at Douai outside the postern gate, shall remain for the uses and according to the customs of those for whom they are known to have been piously built [Col. 1428C].

We therefore decree [Col. 1428D] that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but all things shall be preserved whole, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Laborans, cardinal-priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Saint Callistus. I, Pandulf, cardinal-priest of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. [Col. 1429A] I, Albinus, cardinal-priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Robert, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Peter, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso. I, James, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmidin. I, Gratian, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Gerard, cardinal-deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church, acting as vice-chancellor, [Col. 1429B] on the second day before the Kalends of April, in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1189, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

## CXV. He commands the bishop of Vicenza [Pistori] to investigate whether the sisters of Saint Christina, having destroyed their church, are building another within the city of Treviso against the bishop’s opposition; he is to restrain the nuns.  
*(Lateran, 15 April.)*

[MITTARELLI, *Annals of the Camaldolese*, IV, appendix, p. 176.]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother . . . bishop of Vicenza: greeting and apostolic blessing.

At the report of our beloved sons, the dean and canons of Treviso, we have learned that our venerable [Col. 1429C] brother Conrad, their bishop, at the request of Urban, pope of happy memory, our predecessor, granted certain nuns professing the Camaldolese Order a place outside the walls of the city. There they built a church in honour of God and in memory of blessed Christina. The same bishop often celebrated divine offices in it, and through him many benefices were bestowed upon that place.

But after their abbess had departed this life and been buried there by the sisters, these nuns destroyed the aforesaid church; exhumed the aforesaid abbess; and, without the consent of the canons themselves or of the diocesan bishop, buried her within the city walls, in their parish, in a less suitable place [Col. 1429D]. They are also said to be erecting a church there, disregarding the fact that no one may build a church in their parish without the consent of those canons and the diocesan bishop, save the privileges of the Roman Church. Therefore, since, if what is alleged is true, the audacity of so great a presumption must not be left without due correction, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters diligently to investigate the truth of these matters and, setting aside appeal, to correct and amend by our authority whatever you ascertain has been presumptuously done by the aforesaid nuns.

Given at the Lateran, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of May, in the second year of our pontificate.

## CXVI. He takes the church of Siena under protection and confirms its goods and privileges.  
*(Lateran, 20 April.)*

[LAMI, *Monuments of the Florentine Church*, IV, 9.]

[Col. 1430A]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother BONO, bishop of Siena, and his successors.

Set, though unworthy, by the Lord’s disposition upon the exalted watchtower of the Apostolic See, we are bound to love with brotherly charity our brethren, whether near or far away, and to preserve for the churches in which they are known to serve the Lord their dignity and rights. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, Bishop Bono, we graciously assent to your just requests [Col. 1430B]. Following in the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, the Roman pontiffs Celestine, Eugenius, Anastasius, Adrian, and Alexander, we take under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid Church over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside, and fortify it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that the churches, hospices, and castles, with all goods and possessions which the Church entrusted to you now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter acquire, through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, God granting it, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

[Col. 1430C] Namely, the baptismal churches, with their priories and chapels, which are known to belong to the jurisdiction of the Church entrusted to you: the parish church of Saint Agnes with all its appurtenances; the parish church of Liliano; of Larnano; of Sciara; of Saint Andrew of Bozzone; of Saint Martin in Grania, with every right it possesses in that castle and in Villania; the parish church of Saint Christina of Liciniano; of Saint Perena; of Saint Nazarius; of Saturniano, with every right it has in the church of Saint Mary situated in the borough of Saint Quiricus in Osenna and in the surrounding places; the parish church of Oppiano; of Ancaiano; of Mount Condano; of Saint George in Valona; of Saint Valentine; of Coppiano; [Col. 1430D] of Saint Innocentia; of Carli and Murlo; of Creola; of Saint Christina in Caio; of Montaleino; the church of Saint Mary in the borough of Saint Quiricus; likewise Carcianum, which especially belongs to your governance, care, lordship, and jurisdiction; the title of Saint Angel of Tressa; the parish church of Corsiano; of Ricensa; of Ruscia; of Pentolina; of Sovicille; of Fogliano; of Saint Justus of Casciano; of Marmorala, with all their goods and appurtenances; the castle of Pordano; the castle of Pogna; the castle of Mentido; the castle of Furcole; the castle of Sovicille; the castle of Murlo; the castle of Crevole with the fortress of the same name; the castle of Monteciano with its court and all their appurtenances; what it possesses in the castle of Sylvula; what it possesses in Mount Piscino and in Vallerano; half of Silva; Lake Verrano; half of the lake and marsh of Falano; a fifth part of Aquatico; a fourth part of the tithes and offerings in churches belonging by right to the Church of Siena; a fifth part of Montacutulo, which is above the river Rosia; a third part of the castle and court of Radi in the diocese of Volterra; a fourth part of the castle and court of Valle Aspero in the diocese of Massa, with all appurtenances of the aforesaid portions [Col. 1431A]; also the castles and possessions granted to the Church of Siena by Traduto, son of Count Bernard, both in the counties of Siena, Volterra, Florence, and Fiesole; that which Adolasia of Bibiano gave; that which Rugettus, son of Bernard, gave from his paternal estate; what it possesses from the inheritance of Rolandinus the Lombard; the possessions which it has in the county of the castle of Felicitas; what it has in the castle of Strove and in Castilione; and all castles and possessions which you, or another acting through you, hold in the counties of Siena, Volterra, Florence, Fiesole, and Arezzo. We also confirm by apostolic authority to your devotion the arrangements of the churches situated within your jurisdiction, just as your predecessors possessed them and you yourself have hitherto possessed them [Col. 1431B].

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church [Col. 1431C], take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but all things shall be preserved whole, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, with the authority of the Apostolic See expressly reserved in all respects. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this text of our constitution, should presume rashly to act against it, then, after a second or third admonition, unless he makes due satisfaction and corrects his offence, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But to all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Laborans, cardinal-priest of the church of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of Saint Callistus. I, Pandulf, cardinal-priest of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Albinus, cardinal-priest of the church of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Bobo, cardinal-priest of the church of Saint Anastasia. [Col. 1432A] I, Peter, cardinal-priest of the church of Saint Lawrence in Damaso. I, James, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Gratian, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Gerard, cardinal-deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Octavian, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Goffredus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Bernard, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary the New. I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Agro.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church, acting as vice-chancellor, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of May [Col. 1432B], in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1189, in the second year of the pontificate of Pope Clement III.

## CXVII. He confirms under the protection of the Holy Roman Church the monastery of Subiaco and its goods, which he enumerates; forbids anyone to fish in the monastery’s lake or construct mills without the abbot’s permission; directs that a bishop be sought from the supreme pontiff for consecrations of churches and the ordinations of monks or clerics, but grants leave to receive these from any bishop should the circumstances of the time not permit this; forbids anyone other than the Apostolic See to exercise jurisdiction in that monastery; declares that election of the abbot belongs to the monks and his consecration to the supreme pontiff; establishes penalties against the disobedient; and bestows a blessing upon benefactors.  
*(Lateran, 20 April.)*

[MARGARINI, *Bullar of Cassino*, II, 218.]

[Col. 1432C]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BERALD, abbot of the monastery of Subiaco, and his brethren, present and future, who profess the regular life: in perpetuity.

Although by virtue of the office of administration entrusted to us we are bound to bear care for all churches, we ought nevertheless to have a special concern for those which directly, without any intermediary, belong to the Roman Church, and, with the Lord’s help, to provide for their peace and tranquillity. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and take under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery of Subiaco, which belongs by right to blessed Peter and in which you are devoted to divine service. We fortify it by the privilege of this present document, first decreeing that the monastic order known to have been instituted in that monastery according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, God granting it, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors [Col. 1433A]. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names.

The site in which your monastery stands, with all its appurtenances; the cave in which blessed Benedict dwelt at the beginning of his religious life, together with the adjoining wood, the entire surrounding mountain, and all boundaries or appurtenances established from ancient times; and beneath that same cave, the lake or stream issuing from it. In these waters, indeed, no one may fish or build a mill without the permission of the abbot and brethren, as far as the arch called Ferrata, in the territory of Roviano. Likewise, from the ancient channel which carries water from the river to the parish church of Saint Lawrence, from the water called Augusta, no one may divert water without your permission, except insofar as is sufficient for irrigating the lands and replenishing the baptismal font in that church. Nor may anyone presume to build a water-mill there without your permission, as far as the aforesaid arch of Ferrata. But if anyone acts otherwise, let him be constrained by the ban of the Roman curia; one half of that fine shall be paid to our sacred palace and one half to the same monastery.

We also confirm to you and to your monastery the castle called Subiaco, with all its appurtenances, as is known to have been granted by our predecessors, with mountains and hills, estates and hamlets, and all churches and things belonging to them generally and in their entirety; the estate of Canalis and the estate of Genna in their entirety, with their appurtenances; the estate of Frassinum with all its appurtenances; and the place called Fundi, as it extends to the Emperor’s Rock and goes to the mountain called Pionica, thence by the ridge to Mount Romano, and comes out at Campo Longo, thence to Campo Catinum, then returns to the aforesaid Emperor’s Rock; the place called Seminaria with its boundaries, as is contained in the privilege of our predecessors; the hill of Altulo; the castle of Augusta with its estates and hamlets; the hamlet of Saint Felicitas with that church, its estates and hamlets, and all its appurtenances, as is contained in those same privileges; the fortress of Cervaria with its estates and hamlets and all its appurtenances; the fortress of Incamerata, the castle of Marano, the fortress of Martino, and the fortress of Meso, with all their appurtenances and with the monastery’s ancient inheritance; the castle of Camorano with its fortress, estates, and hamlets; Mount Griffo, the Cold Valley, Mount Meso, and Finistella, with all their appurtenances; the castle of Cerreto with all its appurtenances; the castle of Geramo, with mountains and hills, estates and hamlets, its holdings and all its appurtenances, and with the monastery’s ancient inheritance; the castle of Ampollonio, with its mountains and hamlets; one half of the castle of Sant’Angelo, with its churches, estates, holdings, and appurtenances; the fortress of Santo Stefano with its appurtenances; the valley of Anigno; the cell of Occia, with its mountains, hills, estates, and hamlets; Toccianello; the estate of Orarum; the estate of Microniano; the estate of Caniano; the estate of Convitello; the estate of Acquaviva; and one half of Mount Affilano with all their appurtenances; the castle of Affile, with mountains and hills and one half of Mount Affilano, with all their appurtenances; the castle of Ponzia, with mountains and hills and all its appurtenances; the castle of Roiate with its fortress; moreover, all that is known to belong to the same monastery of Blessed Benedict by ancient right and by grants and privileges of both Roman pontiffs and emperors: the city of Sala, called Carsoli, with its holdings, estates, and hamlets; Auricula; the fortress of Butte; the fortress of Aprunio; Arsule; Roviano; and on the river Anticolo, Saracinisco, the fortress of Miazzi, the fortress of Sunici, Sambuci, Siciliano, one half of Ilice, the holding of Saint Valerius, Piscano, Mount Casale, Civitella, Clibano with all their estates and hamlets; the town of Tusculum with its fortress and all its appurtenances; and the castle of Gallicano with its churches, estates, hamlets, and all its appurtenances.

We also confirm to you the cells belonging to that monastery: namely, the church of Saint Angelo situated at Affile; the church of Saint George with all their appurtenances and with the ancient inheritance of blessed Benedict; the church of Saint Stephen [Col. 1434C] at Piglio; the church of Saint Angelo at Pietralata; Saint Sebastian at Paliano; the churches of Saint Quintinus and Saint Blaise at Anticoli; the church of Saint Leucius at Babuco, with all their appurtenances, situated in the territory of Campagna; at Cartore, the church of Saint Peter at Camerata and Saint Peter of Aprunio; in the Marsican territory, Saint Peter at Nerse, Saint Benedict at the fortress of Meruli, Saint Thomas of Trasacco with the church of Saint Nicholas situated in the village, with their appurtenances; Saint Angelo at Albe; Saint Saviour at Avezzano; Saint Mary of Tufo with its appurtenances; in the Soran valley, the church of Saint Paul with three other churches, with a village situated beside it, and all their appurtenances; [Col. 1434D] Saint John of Pesculo, Saint Mary of Anticoli, Saint Mary of Roviano, Saint Mary of Arsule; in the city of Tivoli, the churches of Saint Antoninus, the Holy Cross, and Saint Barbara, with all their appurtenances; another cell in honour of the Holy Cross at Quintiliano, with its olive grove and its other appurtenances, and six ounces of the church of Saint Peter, with lands and vineyards, as is shown by the ancient boundaries; the village called Papi, with the church of Saint Mary, lands and vineyards, and the mountain called Mansula; the church of Saint Mary situated at the gate; the church of Saint Sebastian with all its appurtenances; three water-mills, one in the old castle, another outside [Col. 1435A] the main gate, and another in Vesta; near the castle of Gallicano, the churches of Saint Pastor, Saint Angelo, Saint Mary, and Saint Lawrence at Acquaalta, with all their possessions; at Rome, the monastery of Saint Erasmus, with the houses, gardens, and other possessions belonging to it.

Furthermore, because of the frequent injuries inflicted upon monasteries by bishops or their officials, we decree that the authority granted to your community by our predecessors shall remain valid for you also: whenever it is expedient to dedicate churches, or to ordain clerics in the monastery, its cells, castles, or villages, you may request a bishop from us. If you cannot come to us in time, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer; supported by the authority of the Apostolic See, he shall perform what is requested, and shall suffer no opposition or complaint concerning this from the bishop of any church. Therefore, we forbid every priest of any church to exercise any jurisdiction in the aforesaid monastery of Blessed Benedict, apart from the Apostolic See. Upon the death of yourself, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any device of fraud or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, have judged, according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict, to be elected; [Col. 1435C] and the person elected shall be consecrated by the Roman pontiff.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those uses for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the customary right of the bishop of Palestrina in Ponzia or Roiate, as is contained in the instrument of settlement made with the consent of both parties. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this document of our constitution, should rashly attempt to contravene it, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the wrong perpetrated; let him be excluded from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church, have signed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the holy Roman Church, acting vice-chancellor, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of May, in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1189, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

## CXVIII. He receives the Church of Ferrara under protection and confirms its possessions and rights.  
*(Lateran, 20 April.)*

[MURATORI, *Antiquities of Italy*, VI, 439.]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable STEPHEN, bishop of Ferrara, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Although, unworthy as we are, by the Lord’s disposition we have been set upon the lofty watchtower of the Apostolic See, we ought to love our brother bishops, both near and far, with fraternal charity and to provide with fatherly concern for the churches entrusted to them by God. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, bishop, we graciously assent to your just requests; following in the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, Innocent, Celestine, Lucius, Alexander, and Gregory, Roman pontiffs, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid Church of Ferrara, over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside, and strengthen it by the privilege of this document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that Church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grant of pontiffs, gift of kings or princes, offering of the faithful, or other just means, by the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Of these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The monastery of Saint Sylvester; the monastery of Saint Bartholomew; the parish church of Saint George beyond the Po; the parish church of Saint Mary of Gabiana; the parish church of Saint Mary of Vicoventia, with the castle and court, and the entire honour and jurisdiction of Vicoventia; the parish church of Saint Martin on the opposite side of the Po; the parish church of Saint Apollinaris of Trisicalio; the parish church of Saint Stephen of Firminiana, with the entire court of Firminiana and Trisicalio, with honour and jurisdiction; the parish church of Saint Peter of Copario; the parish church of Saint George of Tamara; the parish church of Saint Martin of Rupina; the parish church [Col. 1436D] of Saint Mary of the Seven Policini; the parish church of Saint Mary of Vicariano, with the court of Vicariano and all honour and jurisdiction; the parish church of Saint Donatus of Pedrurio, with the court of Saint Donatus and jurisdiction; the parish church of Saint Stephen of Bolonitico, with the court of Bolonitico, honour, and jurisdiction; the parish church of Saint George of Tricenta, with the court of Tricenta, honour, and jurisdiction; the parish church of Saint Antoninus of Ficarolo; the parish church of Saint Mary of Civisello; the parish church of Saint Michael of Brancantino, with the court of Melaria and all honour and jurisdiction; the church of Saint Stephen of Staurano, with its entire court; the church of Saint Romanus of Tartaro; the church of Cadaldo, with its hospital; the church of Saint Thomas, with the hospital below Burana; the church of Saint [Col. 1437A] Matthew, with the hospital of Rupta Petri Scorti; the hospital of All Saints; the hospital of Brother Durancius; the hospital of Caudalonga; the church of Saint Lazarus, with the hospital of the Market Field; the court of Francolino, with all honour and jurisdiction; the courts of Vadrignana and Bragantino, with all honour and jurisdiction; the valley of Theodora; the Duke’s Field; the rise of Pontuaria, with the entire Vallada belonging to it; the church of Saint Martin of Bosco; the hospital of Ruptulo, with all chapels and holdings and their appurtenances.

We therefore confirm to you and your successors by apostolic authority the ancient and reasonable customs which your predecessors have hitherto held in the greater canonry and in the churches of your bishopric. We decree that no one may admit anyone as a canon in the greater church, or to any prelacy, without seeking the counsel and knowledge of you or your successors. Nor may anyone appoint or remove a chaplain in the other churches without your consent. We also grant to you and your successors the free correction of the canons of your church, the other clerics of your bishopric, and monks, and their ordination, just as your predecessors are known to have held it. Moreover, following the example of our aforesaid predecessors, we establish in every respect that the Church of Ferrara, with all its parish, shall be preserved forever in the right, lordship, and privilege [Col. 1437C] of the holy Roman Church of blessed Peter, whose patrimony it is; and that it shall always remain under the election, ordination, and consecration of ourselves and our successors, so that whoever is there elected, ordained, and consecrated may exercise this honour and power in their full integrity. We therefore decree that absolutely no person may, etc.

I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church, have signed. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber and of Calixtus, have signed. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles, have signed. I, Albinus, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have signed. I, Bobo, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have signed. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Damaso, have signed. I, James, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have signed. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have signed. I, Bernard, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, have signed. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have signed. I, Godfrey, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have signed. [Col. 1438A] I, John Felix, cardinal deacon of Saint Eustace beside the temple of Agrippa, have signed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Agro, have signed. I, Bernard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary Nova, have signed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the holy Roman Church acting as vice-chancellor, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of May, in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1189, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

## CXIX. He directs Eberhard, bishop of Merseburg, and Otto, bishop of Eichstätt, to investigate carefully the life and miracles of Otto I, bishop of Bamberg, and, unless they find impediments, to declare him enrolled among the saints.  
*(Lateran, 29 April.)*

[USSERMANN, *Bishopric of Bamberg*, Documents, 133.]

[Col. 1438B]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brethren E., bishop of Merseburg, and O., bishop of Eichstätt; and to the beloved sons, the abbots of Saint Emmeram at Regensburg and of Schwarzach, and the dean and scholasticus of Würzburg: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has come to the hearing of our Apostolic See, from the tenor of certain letters and the report of many persons, that divine power, through the merits and intercession of blessed Otto, formerly bishop of Bamberg, has wrought much salvation, especially among the Pomeranian people, to whom he was sent by the Apostolic See; and there the Lord granted him to shine forth in many miracles. Since, therefore, according to the testimony of Holy Scripture, a lamp is to be set not under a bushel but upon a lampstand, we command your discernment by apostolic letters to inquire more diligently into his life and miracles, which have been reported to us by the letters of many persons. If you find nothing that stands in the way, relying on apostolic authority, solemnly and publicly proclaim him canonized, appointing and publicly announcing that the anniversary day of his passing is to be observed in solemn commemoration, to the honour of God and in memory of that blessed man.

Given at the Lateran, on the third day before the Kalends of May, in the second year of our pontificate.

## CXX. He informs Otto II, bishop of Bamberg, of the mandate given to the bishops of Merseburg and Eichstätt.  
*(Lateran, 1 May.)*

[Ibid.]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother OTTO, bishop, and to the beloved sons, the canons and all the clergy and people of Bamberg and Mount Saint Michael: greeting and apostolic blessing.

When matters are reported to the Apostolic See which concern the salvation of souls and are shown by clear indications to look toward the devotion of clergy and people, we willingly hear them as is fitting, and grant the apostolic favour and assent necessary for their advancement in the Lord. Thus it is that, since it has come to the hearing of our Apostolic See from the tenor of certain letters and from the report of many persons that divine power, through the miracles and intercession of blessed Otto, formerly bishop of Bamberg, has wrought the salvation of many, especially among the Pomeranian people to whom he was sent by the Apostolic See, and among whom the Lord God granted him to shine forth through many miracles—

Having gladly heard these things and rendered thanks to almighty God for such great benefits, and desiring to satisfy your pious wishes for the praise of God, we have commanded our venerable brethren, the bishops of Merseburg [Col. 1439B] and Eichstätt, and our beloved sons, the abbots of Saint Emmeram at Regensburg and of Schwarzach, and the dean and scholasticus of Würzburg, diligently to investigate his life and miracles, which were reported to us in the letters of many persons. If nothing is found that stands in the way, these eminent persons are to proclaim him solemnly and publicly canonized, relying on apostolic authority, appointing and publicly announcing that the anniversary day of his passing be observed in solemn commemoration to the honour of God and in memory of that blessed man.

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of May, in the second year of our pontificate.

## CXXI. He confirms to the monastery of Saint Denis the church of Saint Blaise of Grandpuits.  
*(Lateran, 18 May.)*

[DOUBLET, *History of Saint Denis*, 525.]

[Col. 1439C]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the abbot and brethren of Saint Denis: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners and, where wishes do not depart from the path of reason, bring them to fulfilment with effective action. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, concurring with grateful assent, we confirm to you and your church by apostolic authority, and fortify by the protection of this document, the church of Saint Blaise of Grandpuits with its appurtenances, which Hevardus, the devout founder of the same church, with the assent and confirmation [Col. 1439D] of the venerable brother William, archbishop of Sens, gave to you, just as you possess it justly and peaceably. Moreover, by the authority of these present letters, we grant you that, if a general interdict be imposed upon the land, provided that you yourselves have not been interdicted for your own offence, you may celebrate divine offices there with closed doors, excluding the excommunicated and interdicted, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice; and you may commit members of your household to ecclesiastical burial unless they are excommunicated or interdicted. Therefore, let absolutely no person infringe this document of our confirmation and concession, or rashly oppose it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of June, in the second year of our pontificate.

## CXXII. He receives under protection the monastery of Saint Matthew of Castello, and confirms its discipline, goods, and rights.  
*(Lateran, 12 June.)*

[GATTULA, *History of Cassino*, 403.]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons JACOB, abbot of the monastery of Saint Matthew of the servants of God at Castello, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

[Col. 1440B] Although unworthy, established by the Lord’s bounty upon the lofty watchtower of the Apostolic See, we ought to extend the gaze of our concern to the whole body of the Church and to provide with especially attentive care for the peace of God’s servants. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests, and, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, Alexander and Lucius, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this document. First, we decree that the monastic order known to be established in your monastery according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall be observed there inviolably for all time. Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grant of pontiffs, gift of kings or princes, offering of the faithful, or other just means, by the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Of these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names.

The place itself where the aforesaid monastery is built, with all its appurtenances; the lands and vineyards which you hold in the territory of Aquino; the possessions and lands which you hold in the land of Saint Benedict, or in the *terragium*; the entitlement to bread and wine which you receive daily from the monastery of Cassino under an ancient grant observed hitherto, and that which you receive from the church of Saint Mary of Albaneta and Saint Nicholas of Ciconia, as the aforesaid monastery of Cassino granted you in perpetuity, out of pious regard, to hold. We likewise confirm to you and to your monastery by apostolic authority the liberty granted to your monastery, with the assent of the chapter, by Raynald, Theodinus, Peter, and our beloved son Roffridus, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Marcellinus and Peter, abbots of Cassino of good memory, as is contained in their authentic documents; the good customs observed hitherto; and also the church of Saint Martin of Montemontano, the church of Saint Leonard beside Mount Sambuco with its appurtenances, and the church of Saint Mary of Radicclo with its appurtenances, reasonably granted to you by those same abbots, together [Col. 1441A] with the men whom you hold from the aforesaid monastery of Cassino. You may also receive free and absolved fugitive clerics or laymen for conversion, and retain them in your monastery without any opposition. We further forbid any of your brethren, after having made profession in your house, to leave that house without permission of his abbot. No one may dare retain a departing monk without a certificate from your community. We also forbid anyone to introduce any monk into the same house against your will, or, while you are willing, to remove any of your brethren from it without reasonable cause. Certainly, no one at all may presume to exact tithes from you on your newly cleared land which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the food of your animals. We further decree that no one whatsoever may impose unjust exactions or new rents upon your monastery, or increase the old ones contrary to the statutes of the sacred canons. We also decree that the burial-place of that house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last wishes of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or interdicted, while preserving, however, the right of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. Upon the death of yourself, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any device of fraud or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, have judged, according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict, to be elected.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved whole and unimpaired for the benefit in every way of those uses for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the due right and reverence of the monastery of Cassino. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this document of our constitution, should rashly attempt [Col. 1441D] to contravene it, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by worthy satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the wrong perpetrated; let him be excluded from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to divine vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church, have signed. I, Albanus, bishop of Albano, have signed. [Col. 1442A] I, Bobo, bishop of the see of Porto and Santa Rufina, have signed. I, Octavianus, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, have signed. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus, have signed. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Jordan, cardinal priest of Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor. I, John, cardinal of the title of Saint Clement and bishop of Tusculum, have signed. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have signed. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. [Col. 1442B] I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, have signed. I, Godfrey, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have signed. I, Berard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary Nova, have signed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the holy Roman Church, acting vice-chancellor, on the second day before the Ides of June, in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1189, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

## CXXIII. He absolves the entire chapter of Trier and all clergy and people dwelling throughout the archbishopric from obedience, in spiritual and temporal matters, to Archbishop Folmar and Provost R.  
*(Lateran, 26 June.)*

[GUENTHER, *Rhenish-Moselle Diplomatic Codex*, I, 459.]

[Col. 1442C]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the whole chapter of the Church of Trier, and all clergy and people dwelling throughout the archbishopric of Trier: greeting and apostolic blessing.

With fatherly sympathy for the many burdens of disturbance which the Church has suffered owing to disagreement over the election of the archbishop of Trier, and also considering how many and how great injuries might come to the universal Church from the discord which had arisen between the Roman Church and the empire on this account, from the beginning of our promotion we have laboured without interruption, through ourselves, our brethren, and our legates, with all the zeal and care that we could, so that the aforesaid evils might proceed no further and those which had been stirred up might be stilled. Since the negotiation for this peace and the conclusion of the whole affair required the presence of our venerable brother Folmar, your archbishop, we took care to summon him to us by authority of an apostolic command, after full security had been obtained for him from our dearest sons in Christ, F., emperor, and H., his son, king of the Romans, ever august. [Col. 1443A] Our beloved sons P., cardinal priest of the title of Saint Peter in Chains, and J., cardinal priest of Saint Pudentiana, legates of the Apostolic See, likewise took care to enjoin this very thing upon him on our and their behalf, by letters sent, with all the strictness they could employ. It was also announced that, unless he presented himself before us by the day before the Ides of February now past, we would nevertheless take care to proceed to the conclusion of the affair with the counsel of our brethren. Since, therefore, we do not hitherto know with what intention or obstinacy he has refused to present himself before us, by the authority we exercise, with the common counsel of our brethren, we deprive him, as contumacious and disobedient, of that power which he has hitherto possessed by right of the archbishopric over you, the Church of Trier, its suffragans, and the whole archbishopric. We decree that henceforth both you and the whole archbishopric shall be wholly and permanently absolved, in spiritual and temporal matters insofar as archiepiscopal right is concerned, from obedience to him and to Provost R.; as had been agreed and established at Verona, while Urban, our predecessor of good memory, was still living, between him and the imperial envoys, as appears in the letters of settlement authenticated by the seals of the aforesaid cardinal legates, our venerable brethren the bishop of Bamberg and G., bishop of Würzburg, and our beloved son the abbot of Hersfeld. Nevertheless, we will and command that the prebends and benefices which each of them, and the clerics expelled because of Folmar, possessed at the time [Col. 1443C] of that election, shall be paid to all without any diminution. We wish, indeed, that Folmar aforesaid shall be honourably provided for elsewhere by the Apostolic See. We also forbid that the same Folmar shall ever at any time exercise a legation in the whole diocese of Trier or minister with pontifical insignia. But if the said Folmar, on account of obedience not rendered to him, has deposed, excommunicated, suspended from office, or deprived of benefice any persons, we decree that they are restored in full. Therefore, let absolutely no person infringe this document of our constitution or rashly oppose it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

I, Clement, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Albinus, bishop of Albano. I, Bobo, bishop of the see of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Octavianus, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus. I, Jordan, cardinal priest of Saint Pudentiana, of the title of the Passion. I, John, cardinal of the title of Saint Clement and bishop of Tusculum. [Col. 1444A] I, James, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Godfrey, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the holy Roman Church, acting vice-chancellor, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of June, in the seventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1189, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Clement III.

## CXXIV. He confirms to the monastery of Saint Chrysogonus at Zadar the church of Saint Martin.  
*(Lateran, 28 June.)*

[FARLATI, *Sacred Illyricum*, V, 65.]

[Col. 1444B]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons G. . . . . abbot and brethren: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners and bring to fulfilment with effective action the wishes which do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, concurring with grateful assent in your just requests, we confirm to you and, through you, to the same monastery, by apostolic authority, and fortify by the protection of this document, the church of Saint Martin with all its appurtenances, granted to your monastery by a pious gift from the patrons of that church with the consent of the chapter of Zadar, just as you possess it lawfully and without dispute. We decree that absolutely no person may infringe this document of our confirmation or rashly oppose it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Kalends of July, in the second year of our pontificate.

## CXXV. He confirms to Master Herman and the brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem the gifts which Philip, archbishop of Cologne, had made to the Hospital of the Holy Sepulchre at Duisburg.  
*(Lateran, 14 July.)*

[LACOMBLET, *Charters*, I, 362.]

[Col. 1444D]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons HERMAN, master, and the brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We saw the authentic instrument of our venerable brother Philip, Archbishop of Cologne, from the tenor of which it became known to us that the same archbishop, by pious donation, granted to your hospital of the Holy Sepulchre at Duisburg the house of Conrad de Dicke, the house of Alexander son of Lodewicus, the house of Lanthfrid Brunckini Sifredi, with the intervening spaces, and likewise all the boundaries lying toward the church of St Mary, [Col. 1445A] within the wall and outside the wall of the city, on this condition: namely, that the inhabitants of the aforesaid houses shall receive baptism, burial, visitation of the sick, together with every parochial right, in that hospital house; nevertheless, as formerly, they are bound to attend the synods appointed by the pastor of the church of St Saviour, the archdeacon of Xanten, and the provost of St Cunibert, who is set over that church by right of the deanery.

The same archbishop further ordained that the tithes of animals, together with the pennies popularly called *Orkemscherf*, from the aforesaid houses should be delivered to the aforesaid church of Blessed Mary; in compensation for these, half a mark must be paid yearly to the pastor of the church of St Saviour. Priest A. also, and his successors, shall, all objection being removed, pay a third part of the cathedraticum due to [Col. 1445B] the aforesaid archbishop, and of the service due to the archdeacon of Xanten and the provost of St Cunibert.

Therefore, in order that the ordinance and grant or confirmation of the aforesaid archbishop may obtain the force of stability, we hold it ratified, as it was reasonably made and is contained in his authentic instrument; and, since you possess all the aforesaid peacefully, we confirm it to your devotion by apostolic authority and strengthen it by the protection of this writing. We decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever to infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul. [Col. 1445C]

Given at the Lateran, 14 July, in the second year of our pontificate.

### CXXVI. To the canons of the church of St Thomas of the Louvre at Paris, he confirms the possessions bestowed by Count Robert. (Lateran, 26 July.)

[Dom FÉLIBIEN, *History of Paris*, III, 75.]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of the church of St Thomas of the Louvre: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant our assent to the just desires of petitioners, and bring to fulfilment, by a corresponding effect, vows which do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, yielding to the prayers of the noble lady, the Countess of Brie, [Col. 1445D] we confirm by apostolic authority to your church, and strengthen by the protection of this writing, the possessions and revenues granted as alms to your church by Count Robert, formerly her husband, with her and her children: namely, the court in which stables had been built, so that a hospital might be constructed there; the part of the orchard—commonly called *du verger*—adjoining the hospital and the canons, from the cloister before the church door to the end of the wall; revenues for the support of the resident priest-canons, from the tithes of Torcy, Galliaco, and Brie; and one hundred Parisian pounds, to be paid yearly at Villeneuve-Saint-Georges on the feast of St Remigius; likewise the vineyard and arpent of land situated outside the walls of the aforesaid place of St Thomas—as you possess them justly and without dispute, and as they are contained in [Col. 1446A] their authentic instrument; we confirm them to your church by apostolic authority and strengthen them by the protection of this writing.

We decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever to infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, 26 July, in the second year of our pontificate.

### CXXVII. To the provost and brethren of the church of St Nicholas at Stendal, he grants privileges. (Lateran, 11 September.)

[RIEDEL, *Codex diplomaticus Bremensis*, I, V, 22.]

[Col. 1446B]

CLEMENT, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the provost and brethren of St Nicholas at Stendal.

[lacuna] Yielding to both your prayers and those of our beloved son, the nobleman Count Henry, founder of your church, we have thought fit by this present document to grant to you and your successors that, if your diocesan, having been repeatedly and duly requested by you in humility before prudent men as witnesses, does not grant you ecclesiastical sacraments freely and without any difficulty or improper impediment, you may request them from whichever Catholic bishop possessing the favour of the Apostolic See you prefer; and that bishop, relying on our authority, may provide what is requested.

[Col. 1446C] Let no person whatsoever therefore be permitted, etc.

Given at the Lateran, 11 September, in the second year of our pontificate.

### CXXVIII. To all bishops, he commands that, when requested by the brethren of the church of St Nicholas at Stendal, they administer the sacraments without delay and without appeal. (Lateran, 11 September.)

[Ibid.]
